title: Coding agents
text: PocketOne is new, so coding agents haven't seen much of it. Two things close that gap. Both are built from these docs, so they change when the docs change.

title: Coding agents
heading: Agent Skills
text: The pocketone plugin has two skills: pocketone: the pocketone binary and its commands, pocketone.yaml , every extension, and writing your own extension with contracts. pocketpages: building PocketPages v1 sites in pb_pages/ : routing, ctx , templates, layouts, auth and deploying. Each skill carries a copy of the docs in its reference/ folder, so it works offline. Claude Code /plugin marketplace add pockethost/pocketone /plugin install pocketone@pocketone /plugin marketplace update pocketone picks up new versions. Other agents that read Agent Skills (Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and others) npx skills add pockethost/pocketone Or copy a skill folder into your project yourself. The skills live in agent/skills/ .

title: Coding agents
heading: llms.txt
text: For agents and tools that read the web: pocketone.dev/llms.txt indexes every docs page with a one-line summary. pocketone.dev/llms-full.txt holds every docs page in one Markdown file. PocketPages has its own at pocketpages.dev/llms.txt and pocketpages.dev/llms-full.txt.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
text: Every section the pocketone binary understands, from pocketone config --json . Each extension owns its own section. pocketone config check checks a file. How the file works (where it's found, .env secrets) is on the Config page.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: app:
text: The single app: data dir, dev mode, encryption, hooks, migrations, public dir, and the .env names it may read (env_allow). Not used on a multisite host. dir string The data folder (pb_data). Default: pb_data next to the executable. The --dir flag wins. dev bool Dev mode: logs and SQL statements printed to the console. The --dev flag wins. encryption_env string Name of the environment variable holding a 32-character key that encrypts the app settings. The --encryptionEnv flag wins. query_timeout duration Default timeout for SELECT queries, such as 30s. The --queryTimeout flag wins. hooks_dir string The JS hooks folder. Default: pb_hooks next to pb_data. The --hooksDir flag wins. hooks_watch bool Restart the app when a pb_hooks file changes. On unless false. The --hooksWatch flag wins. jsvm string The JS engine for pb_hooks and pb_migrations: quickjs (PocketOne's, the default) or goja (PocketBase's own, for pure PocketBase compatibility: pages, $mcp, $tokens and JS contracts are off). The --jsvm flag wins. hooks_pool int Only with jsvm: goja: how many JS runtimes are kept ready for hooks. Default 15. The --hooksPool flag wins. migrations_dir string The migrations folder. Default: pb_migrations next to pb_data. The --migrationsDir flag wins. automigrate bool Write a migration file when you change collections in the dashboard. On unless false. The --automigrate flag wins. public_dir string The static files folder. Default: pb_public next to the executable. The --publicDir flag wins. index_fallback bool Serve index.html for a missing static path, for single-page apps. On unless false. The --indexFallback flag wins. env_allow list of string Names from the .env the app and its JS hooks may read. Default none.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: autotls:
text: Automatic HTTPS certificates (ACME): auto, email, CA, domains, DNS-01, certificate storage. The --autotls flags win. auto bool Get certificates through ACME (CertMagic). Flag: --autotls. email string ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. Flag: --autotlsEmail. ca string letsencrypt (default), letsencrypt-staging, zerossl, or an ACME directory URL. Flag: --autotlsCA. storage string Where certificates are kept. Default pb_data/.autotls. domains list of string Extra domains to get at start; wildcards ( .example.com) need dns. Flag: --autotlsDomains. dns.provider string DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges (needed for wildcards): cloudflare. Flag: --autotlsDNS. dns.api_token string The provider's API token. Write $VAR to read it from the .env beside the file. dns.api_token_env string Or: the environment variable holding the token. Default CF_API_TOKEN. Flag: --autotlsDNSTokenEnv. Owned by Auto TLS.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: docker:
text: Runtime provider docker: each instance in its own container with the PocketBase (pb:) or PocketOne (p1:) binary of its version (image, binary cache and manifest, instance root, default version, idle stop, limits). socket string The Docker socket. Default $DOCKER_HOST when it is unix://, else /var/run/docker.sock. image string Base image the binaries run in, such as alpine:3.20. Required; pulled when missing. binaries string Folder of the release binary cache and its releases.json. Required. versions list of string The minors this host serves, such as pb:0.36 or p1:0.0 (latest patch of each, from docker update). root string Folder with one folder per instance ( / ). Required. home string The instance folder inside the container. Default /home/pockethost. default_version string Version for instances that name none, such as p1:0.0. . Empty: such instances fail. min_upstream string Oldest upstream PocketBase release served. Default 0.23.0; lower it only for releases you cache yourself. idle_ttl duration Stop a container after this long without requests. Default 10m. max_concurrent_starts int Containers starting at once. Default 4. start_timeout duration How long a container gets to answer its health check. Default 60s. nano_cpus int CPU limit per container in billionths of a CPU (1000000000 = one CPU). 0: no limit. pids_limit int Process limit per container. 0: Docker's default. nofile list of int Open-file limit per container: [soft, hard]. Empty: Docker's default. cap_drop list of string Linux capabilities to drop, such as [ALL]. no_new_privileges bool Set no-new-privileges on every container. network string Docker network for the containers. Default the bridge. adopt_image string Also adopt running unlabeled containers of this image named after an instance id (taking over from another manager). Owned by Docker.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: edges:
text: The fleet: this edge's id and a fixed list of the other edges (id, internal_url, region). self string This edge's id, such as lax-1. list list of object The other edges: id, internal_url (where this edge reaches it) and optional region. Owned by Edge.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: firewall:
text: Peers allowed to connect, trusted proxies and client-IP headers, trusted clients, the rate-limit header prefix. Turns the firewall on. allow_cidrs list of string Peers (IPs or CIDRs) allowed to connect; others get 403. Empty: everyone. trusted_proxies list of string Peers whose client-IP headers are believed. client_ip_headers list of string Headers read, in order, for the client IP from a trusted proxy. Default CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP. trusted_clients list of string Client IPs or CIDRs that get the trusted rate limits on every instance. trusted_client_headers list of string Headers a trusted client uses to name its end user's IP, so each user gets their own limits. Default X-Client-IP. rate_limit_header_prefix string Prefix of the rate-limit response headers. Default X-RateLimit. Owned by Firewall.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: instances:
text: Where a multi-instance host's instances come from (a YAML file), and dev mode (serve unknown hostnames). file string instances.yaml The instances file (id, hosts and settings for each instance), reloaded when it changes. dev bool Also serve unknown hostnames: each becomes an instance named after it, in dev mode, with its folder made on first use. Owned by Multisite.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: lifecycle:
text: Instance data on this host: how often disk use is measured and last-request times are reported. measure_every duration 24h0m0s How old an instance's disk measurement may get before it is measured again. Default 24h. report_every duration 1h0m0s How often changed last-request times are reported to the sink. Default 1h. concurrency int 2 How many instances are measured at once. Default 2. Owned by Stats.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: mothership:
text: A community mothership to mirror instances and edges from: url, login, this edge's id, internal URL, region, apex. url string The mothership's URL. Required. email string Superuser email this edge logs in with; use a $VAR from the .env. password string Superuser password; use a $VAR from the .env. self string This edge's edge_id, such as lax-1. Default: the edges section's self. Required. internal_url string Where other edges reach this one. Set: the edge registers itself when the mothership has no record for it. region string Region recorded when the edge registers itself. apex string Makes . a hostname of every instance. Empty: hosts only. heartbeat duration How often this edge marks itself online. Default 15s; negative: never. resync duration How often everything is reloaded, in case a change was missed. Default 10m. Owned by Mothership.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: multisite:
text: Serve many instances (a multisite host) instead of a single app. The runtimes are the providers of runtime/v1. Owned by Multisite.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: pitr:
text: Point-in-time restore: on by default, retention, snapshot interval. The --pitr and --pitrRetention flags win. enabled bool On unless false. The --pitr flag wins. retention duration How far back a restore can go. Default 72h. The --pitrRetention flag wins. snapshot_interval duration How often a full copy is taken. Default 24h. Shorter: faster restores, more storage. Owned by PITR.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: pocker:
text: Runtime provider pocker: instances run in-process (root folder, hooks pool, egress allow list, instance limit defaults). root string ./pb_root The folder holding one folder per instance: / . hooks_pool_size int 2 Ignored: each instance has one JS VM (ext/jsvm). Kept so existing configs load. max_js_execution duration 30s Longest any single JS call (hook, route, cron job, migration) may run. max_js_allocation int 67108864 Largest result a JS built-in may allocate in one step, such as 64MiB. max_call_stack_size int 2000 Deepest JS recursion allowed. max_sleep duration 10s Longest a JS sleep() call may wait. max_query_duration duration 30s Longest an SQL statement without its own deadline may run. http_send_max_timeout duration 1m0s Longest timeout a JS $http.send call may use. http_send_max_body int 10485760 Largest response body a JS $http.send call may read, such as 10MiB. max_concurrent_js int 16 JS calls an instance runs at once; more wait up to max_js_execution, then fail. egress_allow list of string Private networks (CIDRs) instances may still connect to. Default none: public addresses only. Owned by Pocker.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: providers:
text: Which extension provides a contract when several do. Owned by Standard Set.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: rate_limits:
text: Default rate limits for every instance (per instance: extensions.firewall.rate_limits). Turns the firewall on. ip_hourly int Requests per hour from one client IP to one instance. Default 1000. instance_hourly int Requests per hour to one instance from everyone. Default 10000. ip_concurrent int Requests one client IP may have open on one instance at once. Default 15. instance_concurrent int Requests one instance may have open at once. Default 250. file_weight number What a /api/files request costs, as a share of a request. Default 0.1. trusted.ip_hourly int Requests per hour from one trusted client IP to one instance. trusted.instance_hourly int Requests per hour to one instance. trusted.ip_concurrent int Requests one trusted client IP may have open on one instance at once. trusted.instance_concurrent int Requests one instance may have open at once. off bool No rate limiting. The default in dev mode unless rate_limits is set. Owned by Firewall.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: s3redirect:
text: Signed S3 redirects for file downloads: enabled, URL lifetime. The --s3Redirect and --s3RedirectTTL flags win. enabled bool On unless false (it only acts when S3 file storage is on). Flag: --s3Redirect. ttl duration How long each signed URL stays valid. Default 5m, max 7 days. Flag: --s3RedirectTTL. Owned by S3 Redirect.

title: pocketone.yaml reference
heading: server:
text: How the binary listens: http, https and CORS origins (single-app mode: the serve command's defaults). http string Plain HTTP address, such as 127.0.0.1:8090. Single app: the --http default (the flag wins). Many instances: redirects to https when https is set. https string HTTPS address. Single app: the --https default (the flag wins). Many instances: the main address. origins list of string Allowed CORS origins. Single app: the --origins default (the flag wins). plain list of string Many instances only: extra plain HTTP addresses with no redirect. tls.cert string Many instances only: the certificate file, reloaded when it changes. tls.key string Many instances only: the private key file, reloaded when it changes. shutdown_timeout duration Many instances only: how long in-flight requests get to finish at stop.

title: All contracts
text: New to the idea? Read How PocketOne fits together first. This page is the list of every contract and how to write one. Every API a PocketOne extension offers is a contract: a versioned Go interface, and the HTTP API, hooks and MCP tools that come with it, at /api/_c/ / . Extensions have no routes of their own. An extension says what it implements , requires and works with in terms of these contracts, never another extension's name, so any extension that implements a contract can stand in for another. PocketOne answers "who provides this contract on this app?" at startup and prints the answer. Every contract lives here, standard or community; extensions live in ext/ . Each contract is a package named for its id and major version: deploy/v1 is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/contracts/deploy/v1 , mail.fallback/v1 is .../mail/fallback/v1 . A change to what a contract promises is a new major version ( v2 ) next to the old one. The table is generated from each contract's README and every extension's Contracts() : run go run ./.github/extensions contracts (CI fails when it's stale). bulkmail/v1 Run bulk mail campaigns: count an audience; start, pause, resume, cancel, preview and test a campaign. bulkmail @benallfree cli.commands/v1 The pocketone command tree: every contract operation as a remote command by default; extensions replace or add commands. @benallfree deploy/v1 A project's code files on an app: check, upload, commit, list, read, write, delete, tree. deploy (default) @benallfree gate/v1 What admits requests on a multisite host: peer checks, client IPs and rate limits, in order. firewall @benallfree http.wrap/v1 Middleware around everything a multisite host serves, nested in order. servertiming @benallfree instance.source/v1 The instance record a multisite host serves, and where the records come from. mothership @benallfree mail.fallback/v1 Where an app's mail goes when SMTP is off: a chain of providers that send it or pass it on. mailrelay, mailtrap @benallfree mail.feedback/v1 Mail providers' reports (bounces, complaints, unsubscribes) received at one place and raised as events any extension can act on. bulkmail (default) @benallfree mail.suppression/v1 Addresses an app must not send bulk mail to, and the unsubscribe link every bulk message carries. bulkmail (default) @benallfree mcp/v1 The app's MCP endpoint at /mcp, with every provided contract's operations as tools. mcp (default) @benallfree oauth/v1 The app's OAuth 2.1 authorization server, so the CLI and MCP clients can sign in. tokens mcp @benallfree remote/v1 Remote control of an app: whoami, status, restart, logs. The base every client starts from. docker, remotes (default) deploy @benallfree restore/v1 Put an app's data back as it was at a moment: from continuous history, or the latest backup before it. backups (default), pitr @benallfree runtime/v1 What runs a multisite host's instances (in-process, in containers), in preference order. docker, pocker @benallfree settings/v1 The settings an app's admins change for its extensions, one API for all of them. settings (default) bulkmail, mailrelay, pitr @benallfree tls/v1 The TLS of a multisite host's listener: automatic certificates instead of certificate files. autotls @benallfree tokens/v1 An app's API tokens: check one, register scopes, read a request's token, limit in-process requests; the token API. tokens deploy, mcp, remotes @benallfree internal/example/v1 is a test-only wire contract that exercises the generated code.

title: All contracts
heading: Three kinds
text: Service: a Go interface, looked up in the same process ( fallbackv1.Contract.Of(app) ). Wire: a service with an HTTP API under /api/_c/ / , generated from its interface: each method is an operation with its own HTTP method, path and token scope ( //op: POST restart scope=remote ); inputs and results are JSON, uploads ( extkit.RawIn ), downloads ( extkit.RawOut ) or streams ( extkit.Stream , sent as server-sent events). It gets action hooks ( remotev1.OnRestart , onRemoteRestart in pb_hooks ), an MCP tool per JSON operation and a client. Every caller (HTTP, MCP, Go) passes the same scope check and hooks. Routed: a contract whose provider is an http.Handler serving everything under /api/_c/ / as it is, for an API a protocol shapes (OAuth) or an existing API moved under a contract (deploy/v1). A multisite host can provide a wire or routed contract for its instances, so it works for instances that run stock PocketBase. A contract can bring its own dashboard screen ( Contract.UI(name, fsys) ): it shows on every app that provides the contract, whichever extension does, and calls only the contract's API. restore/v1's "Restore to a moment" works this way. An extension that calls a contract for its own work (bulk mail checking whoever keeps the suppression list) passes extkit.Internal as the auth, and can ask who provides it with Contract.Provider(app) .

title: All contracts
heading: Add a contract
text: A contract is a folder ext/contracts/ /vN/ ( mail.fallback/v1 → mail/fallback/v1/ ) with: the Go package: the interface, its //contract: directives and zz_contract.go ; a README.md , its page on pocketone.dev, with front matter and four sections in this order: owners: ["@your-github-handle"] summary: "One line: what the contract promises." # mail.fallback/v1 ## Use how to call it: HTTP, Go, pb_hooks, MCP, CLI ## Provide how to implement it ## Extensions (generated: who provides, requires and works with it) ## License MIT Whoever first creates a contract owns it; an extension author who adds one owns both the contract and the extension that provides it. Ids are unique across PocketOne. Pick a name for what the contract does ( restore/v1 ), not for the extension that first provides it.

title: All contracts
heading: Write the interface
text: A contract is an interface with //contract: directives; contractgen writes the rest ( zz_contract.go ) with go generate ./... . A test fails when a generated file is stale. //go:generate go run github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/contracts/cmd/contractgen // Deployer sends a project's code to an app. // //contract:id deploy/v1 //contract:kind wire //contract:scope deploy //contract:host //contract:js hooks type Deployer interface { // Upload writes changed files to the app. Upload(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in UploadInput) (UploadResult, error) } Methods take ctx , then (wire) extkit.Auth , then at most one input; they return error or one value and error . The doc comment of a wire method is its MCP tool's description. Contracts are reviewed like PocketOne's core: a contract is a promise every implementation keeps.

title: All contracts
heading: Use one
text: // provide (in Register) deployv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, myDeployer{}) // consume (after registration: in hooks, at serve time) d := deployv1.Contract.Must(app) // declare it, so PocketOne can order and switch extensions func (e Extension) Contracts() extkit.Contracts { return extkit.Contracts{Implements: extkit.IDs("deploy/v1"), Defaults: extkit.IDs("deploy/v1")} } Choose between providers in pocketone.yaml : providers: mail.fallback/v1: mailrelay

title: All contracts
heading: License
text: MIT

title: bulkmail/v1
text: Campaigns to many recipients, sent at a pace the app's mail account can take. Campaigns are records in the provider's collection, created and edited with PocketBase's records API; this contract runs them. The list of addresses never to mail is mail.suppression/v1; providers' bounce and complaint reports are mail.feedback/v1. A wire contract (bulkmail.go).

title: bulkmail/v1
heading: Use
text: Count /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/count {"audience": {...}} bulkmail:read Start /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/start {"campaign": " ", "limit": 0} bulkmail Pause, Resume, Cancel /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/pause ( resume , cancel ) {"campaign": " "} bulkmail Preview /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/preview {"campaign": " ", "email": ""} bulkmail:read Test /api/_c/bulkmail/v1/test {"campaign": " ", "to": ""} bulkmail Campaign actions answer {"campaign": } . The audience's shape is the provider's (see Bulk Mail). Only superusers may call these. Agents get them as MCP tools ( bulkmail_start , ...); pb_hooks can hook each ( onBulkmailStart ).

title: bulkmail/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement bulkmailv1.Campaigns and provide it in your extension's Register .

title: bulkmail/v1
heading: Extensions
text: bulkmail provides

title: bulkmail/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: cli.commands/v1
text: The pocketone command tree. Every operation of every wire contract linked into the binary is a command under remote , with no code: pocketone remote restore to --at -2h calls restore/v1's RestoreTo on the project's remote. An extension replaces one of those commands by providing the same path, or adds commands of its own. One provider per path; when two extensions provide the same path, pocketone.yaml picks one. A keyed contract (by command path), in the developer's pocketone process (commands.go).

title: cli.commands/v1
heading: Use
text: The generated commands, for any contract: Path: remote , the contract id's words, then the operation: restore/v1's restore_to is remote restore to , mail.suppression/v1's check is remote mail suppression check , remote/v1's status is remote status ( clicmdv1.PathOf ). Flags: one per field of the operation's input ( --at , --email , --campaign ), plus --json for the whole input ( @file , - for stdin) and --remote (a remote's name or a URL; default: the project's default remote). Times take RFC 3339, a local time ( 2026-11-10 15:00 ) or a duration from now ( -2h ). Output: the answer as JSON; streams print one JSON line per entry until Ctrl-C. Auth: the remote's saved login ( pocketone login ), or P1_TOKEN in CI. Not commands: public operations that take or return a raw body (an unsubscribe page, a mail provider's webhook); they're for browsers and services. A remote that doesn't offer the contract answers "this remote doesn't offer restore/v1".

title: cli.commands/v1
heading: Provide
text: Provide a command in your extension's Register . The same path as a generated command replaces it; a new path adds one: clicmdv1.Contract.Provide(app, clicmdv1.Command{ Path: "remote rehash", Short: "Rehash every stored password", Flags: func(fs pflag.FlagSet) { fs.Bool("dry-run", false, "only count") }, Run: func(c clicmdv1.Ctx, args []string) error { caller, err := c.Caller("rehash/v1") // the command's remote, with its login if err != nil { return err } return caller.Call(c, "POST", "", nil, nil) }, }) and declare Implements: extkit.IDs("cli.commands/v1") . Two providers of one path fail the start until pocketone.yaml picks: providers: cli.commands/v1: remote rehash: rehasher A binary builds its tree with clicmdv1.Mount(app, rootCmd) once the app's contracts are sealed; the standard set does it in Register . Commands already on the tree ( remote add , remote whoami ) stay unless a provider replaces them.

title: cli.commands/v1
heading: Extensions
text: No extension declares this contract yet.

title: cli.commands/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: deploy/v1
text: A project's code on an app: pb_hooks , pb_migrations , pb_public and packages. Clients send only the files the app lacks, then swap the new set in at once. Restart and logs are remote/v1's, which it requires. A routed contract (deploy.go): its provider is an http.Handler serving the file API below. A multisite host can provide it for its instances.

title: deploy/v1
heading: Use
text: POST /api/_c/deploy/v1/check which files the app lacks (JSON) POST /api/_c/deploy/v1/blobs upload them (gzip bytes) POST /api/_c/deploy/v1/commit swap the new code set in (JSON) GET /api/_c/deploy/v1/files list deployed files DELETE /api/_c/deploy/v1/files delete files GET / PUT /api/_c/deploy/v1/files/raw read or write one file (raw bytes) GET /api/_c/deploy/v1/tree the app's code tree, for two-way sync Token scopes: deploy (everything) and deploy:read (list, read, tree). The CLI: pocketone deploy , dev , pull .

title: deploy/v1
heading: Provide
text: Provide an http.Handler that serves the API under deployv1.Prefix : deployv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, handler) A host provides it for its instances with deployv1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(host, factory) and extkit.HostRoutes(host, deployv1.Contract, multisite.InstanceID, next) in its instance routes ( multisite.Host.InstanceRoutes , after the gates).

title: deploy/v1
heading: Extensions
text: deploy provides (default)

title: deploy/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: gate/v1
text: What admits requests on a multisite host before an instance is served here or forwarded to another server: a peer allow list, the real client IP behind a proxy, rate limits. Gates run in order and every one must admit; a gate may answer the request itself (429, 403). A host-scope service contract, many providers in order (gate.go).

title: gate/v1
heading: Use
text: Nothing to call: the host runs every gate on every request. Pick or order them in pocketone.yaml : providers: gate/v1: [firewall]

title: gate/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement gatev1.Gate ( AllowPeer before routing, Admit per instance, returning a release function), and gatev1.ClientIPResolver if the gate knows the real client. Provide it in a host extension's RegisterHost : gatev1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myGate)

title: gate/v1
heading: Extensions
text: firewall provides

title: gate/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: http.wrap/v1
text: Middleware around everything a multisite host serves: health, every instance, forwarded requests. Wrappers nest in provider order, the first outermost (a Server-Timing header first, so it measures everything inside it). A host-scope service contract, many providers in order (wrap.go).

title: http.wrap/v1
heading: Use
text: Nothing to call: the host wraps its handler with every provider. Order them in pocketone.yaml if needed: providers: http.wrap/v1: [servertiming]

title: http.wrap/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement wrapv1.Wrapper ( Wrap(next http.Handler) http.Handler ) and provide it in a host extension's RegisterHost : wrapv1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myWrapper)

title: http.wrap/v1
heading: Extensions
text: servertiming provides

title: http.wrap/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: Contracts: how PocketOne fits together
text: PocketOne is PocketBase plus extensions. What keeps those extensions from turning into a pile of plugins that know too much about each other is how they meet: through contracts .

title: Contracts: how PocketOne fits together
heading: The idea
text: A contract is a promise with a name and a version. restore/v1 promises one thing: put this app's data back as it was at a moment . It says what you can ask and what you get back. It says nothing about how. An extension that keeps the promise provides the contract. Everything else talks to the contract, never to the extension behind it: the dashboard, the pocketone command, an AI agent over MCP, your pb_hooks , and other extensions. That's the whole rule: every API an extension offers is a contract. Extensions have no private routes and never import each other.

title: Contracts: how PocketOne fits together
heading: An example: restore/v1
text: Every PocketOne app can restore its data to a moment. Who does the work depends on the app: PITR Any second in the last three days, from continuous history. Backups, the default The latest backup made at or before the moment. It steps aside when PITR is on. A multisite host It could restore an instance from the host's own disk snapshots. Asking looks the same whoever answers: pocketone remote restore to --at -2h # the command line curl -X POST https://app.example.com/api/_c/restore/v1/restore \ -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" -d '{"at": "2026-11-10T15:00:00Z"}' # HTTP An agent asked to "restore my app to yesterday at 3pm" calls the same operation as an MCP tool. Settings → Backups shows the contract's own "Restore to a moment" screen. The answer always says which point the data came from: exactly 3pm with PITR, or the 2:00 backup without it. If something better than PITR comes along tomorrow, it provides restore/v1 , and nothing that restores apps has to change.

title: Contracts: how PocketOne fits together
heading: Why it matters
text: Swap anything. Any extension that provides a contract can stand in for another. One line in pocketone.yaml chooses when several could. Build on anything. Extensions depend on contracts, not on each other: Deploy requires remote/v1 , not "the Remotes extension". Replace Remotes and Deploy keeps working. One surface, promised. If a client can call it, it's in a contract: named, versioned, documented and checked. Every extension route lives under /api/_c/ / ; only paths a standard fixes stay at the root ( /.well-known/ , /mcp ). Written once, reachable everywhere. A contract's interface is the source for everything around it. Each operation is at once an HTTP endpoint, a pocketone remote command, an MCP tool, a hook in Go and in pb_hooks , and a typed client call. Every one of those paths passes the same checks: superusers only unless the operation is public, the token's scopes, and the action hooks. Nothing hidden. Each app prints who provides what when it starts; pocketone remote whoami lists the contracts an app offers; the catalogue lists every contract with the extensions that provide it, require it and work with it.

title: Contracts: how PocketOne fits together
heading: What one interface gives you
text: Write the interface, run go generate , and a contract like restore/v1 gets all of this: HTTP API GET /api/_c/restore/v1 , POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore Command line pocketone remote restore points , pocketone remote restore to --at -2h MCP tools restore_points , restore_restore_to Hooks restorev1.OnRestoreTo(app, ...) in Go, onRestoreRestoreTo(...) in pb_hooks Client restorev1.NewClient(url, token, nil).RestoreTo(...) Dashboard "Restore to a moment" on Settings → Backups, shown for any provider

title: Contracts: how PocketOne fits together
heading: Who provides what
text: When an app starts, PocketOne settles every contract and says what it decided: standard: restore/v1 ← pitr (default backups stepped aside) standard: mail.fallback/v1 ← mailtrap standard: deploy/v1 ← deploy (default) Defaults. A standard extension often provides a contract as the default: it steps aside as soon as anything else provides it. Choices. When two extensions provide a contract that takes one, the app won't start until pocketone.yaml picks one: providers: restore/v1: pitr Chains. Some contracts take several providers in order. Mail with SMTP off goes through mail.fallback/v1 's chain: the dev inbox in dev mode, then a host's relay. Your own JS. An app's pb_hooks can provide contracts too, in onContracts((e) = e.provide(...)) . The host. On a multisite host, some contracts are answered by the host for its instances. An instance running a stock PocketBase image in Docker has no PocketOne extensions inside it, but the host still answers remote/v1 for it, so pocketone remote logs works there too. The host's own parts are contracts as well: what runs instances ( runtime/v1 , Pocker or Docker), what admits requests ( gate/v1 ), its TLS ( tls/v1 ).

title: Contracts: how PocketOne fits together
heading: Versions
text: A contract's id carries its major version only: restore/v1 . Within v1 the promise doesn't change. Changing it means a restore/v2 beside v1 , so whatever relies on v1 keeps working. A new optional ability is usually a new, small contract rather than a change to an old one.

title: Contracts: how PocketOne fits together
heading: Where contracts live, and who owns them
text: Every contract, from the standard set or the community, lives in one place: ext/contracts/ /vN/ ( mail.fallback/v1 is ext/contracts/mail/fallback/v1/ ). Extensions live in ext/ / . Keeping contracts together means one namespace, so two authors can't publish different rehash/v1 s, and it means one place to look for what you can build on. Each contract has a README like an extension's, with its owners and a one-line promise at the top. Its list of the extensions that provide it, require it and work with it is generated from the code, so it's never out of date. Whoever first creates a contract owns it. An extension author who needs a contract that doesn't exist yet writes it first, and then owns both the contract and the extension that provides it. Changes to a contract are reviewed carefully, because every provider and every caller relies on the promise. Name a contract for what it does ( restore/v1 ), not for the extension that happens to provide it first.

title: Contracts: how PocketOne fits together
heading: Words
text: Contract A named, versioned promise: a Go interface plus the API, commands, tools and hooks generated from it. Provide An extension keeps the promise for an app. Require An extension can't work without the contract; without a provider it's turned off, and the startup lines say why. Works with An extension uses the contract when something provides it. Default A provider that steps aside when any other extension provides the contract. Host-provided A multisite host answers the contract for its instances.

title: Contracts: how PocketOne fits together
heading: Next
text: All contracts: what each one promises, and who provides, requires and works with it. Writing an extension: declare, provide and use contracts in your extension. Add a contract: the folder, the README and the generated code.

title: instance.source/v1
text: The record of one instance on a multisite host: its id, hostnames, PocketBase version, folder, secrets, limits, superusers, per-extension settings, whether it's blocked or runs elsewhere. Every host contract reads the same record: runtimes run it, gates admit requests for it. A source supplies the records and streams changes. A host-scope service contract (instance.go, limits.go).

title: instance.source/v1
heading: Use
text: A host takes its records from whichever extension provides this contract: by default its instances file ( instances: { file: instances.yaml } ), or a control plane's mirror (ext/mothership). In Go the record is sourcev1.Instance ( multisite.Instance is the same type).

title: instance.source/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement sourcev1.Source : Snapshot(ctx) returns every instance, Watch(ctx) streams changes (upserts and deletes) until ctx is done. Provide it on the host's scope in a host extension's RegisterHost : sourcev1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, mySource)

title: instance.source/v1
heading: Extensions
text: mothership provides

title: instance.source/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: mail.fallback/v1
text: Where an app's mail goes when its SMTP is off. Providers form an ordered chain: each sends a message or passes it on; when all pass, PocketBase sends it its own way ( sendmail ). An app with SMTP on never reaches the chain. A service (fallback.go), many providers, open to pb_hooks .

title: mail.fallback/v1
heading: Use
text: Nothing to call: mail an app sends with SMTP off goes through the chain. Order the providers in pocketone.yaml : providers: mail.fallback/v1: [mailtrap, mailrelay]

title: mail.fallback/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement fallbackv1.Sender ( Send(ctx, mailer.Message) , returning fallbackv1.ErrPass to pass), provide it, and bind the chain once: fallbackv1.Contract.Provide(app, mySender{}) fallbackv1.Bind(app) From pb_hooks : onContracts((e) = { e.provide("mail.fallback/v1", { send(m) { if (!m.to.some((a) = a.address.endsWith("@example.com"))) throw new ContractError("pass") // send it your way }, }) e.next() })

title: mail.fallback/v1
heading: Extensions
text: mailrelay provides mailtrap provides

title: mail.fallback/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: mail.feedback/v1
text: What mail providers report back about mail an app sent: bounces, spam complaints, unsubscribes. The provider of this contract receives the reports and raises one event per address; any number of extensions act on them through one hook. A suppression list adds the address, a CRM marks the contact, pb_hooks logs it. A wire contract (feedback.go). Its operations are public: SES messages are checked by their SNS signature, webhook calls by a shared secret.

title: mail.feedback/v1
heading: Use
text: SES POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/ses an Amazon SNS HTTPS subscription for SES bounce and complaint notifications Webhook POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/webhook with X-Feedback-Secret any provider: {"type": "bounce\ complaint\ unsubscribe", "email": "...", "campaign": "..."} Act on the events in Go: feedbackv1.OnEvent(app).BindFunc(func(e feedbackv1.Event) error { // e.Kind: bounce, complaint or unsubscribe; e.Email, e.Campaign, e.Source return e.Next() })

title: mail.feedback/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement feedbackv1.Receiver : check each report, then call feedbackv1.Raise(app, &feedbackv1.Event{...}) for each address. Where the webhook secret comes from is the provider's (Bulk Mail keeps it in its settings).

title: mail.feedback/v1
heading: Extensions
text: bulkmail provides (default)

title: mail.feedback/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: mail.suppression/v1
text: The addresses an app must not send bulk mail to (unsubscribed, bounced, complained, added by hand), and the unsubscribe link in every bulk message. Anything that mails many people checks it. A wire contract (suppression.go).

title: mail.suppression/v1
heading: Use
text: Check GET /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/check?email= superusers ( suppression:read ) Suppress POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/suppress {"email", "reason", "source", "campaign"} superusers ( suppression ) Unsuppress POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsuppress {"email"} superusers ( suppression ) UnsubscribePage GET /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe?t= public: the link in a message Unsubscribe POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe public: the page's form, or a mail provider's one-click POST Reasons: unsubscribed , bounced , complained , manual . The page never unsubscribes on a GET (link scanners open every URL in a message); one-click unsubscribes follow RFC 8058 ( List-Unsubscribe=One-Click ). The token is signed by the provider, so only links it issued work.

title: mail.suppression/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement suppressionv1.List ; sign the tokens in the links your messages carry, and point List-Unsubscribe at /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe?t=... .

title: mail.suppression/v1
heading: Extensions
text: bulkmail provides (default)

title: mail.suppression/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: mcp/v1
text: The app's Model Context Protocol endpoint, so agents (a Claude connector, Claude Code, any Streamable HTTP client) can work with it. It stays at /mcp : people paste that URL, MCP versions itself in the protocol, and OAuth tokens are bound to the resource URL. What every provider serves the same way, the contract owns: The routes: /mcp , and its protected resource metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp . The tools: every wire contract the app provides, one tool per operation ( restore_points , bulkmail_start , ...), with an input schema from the operation's types and called through the contract, so the same superuser check, scopes and hooks apply as over HTTP; and tools extensions add with AddTool . A provider brings the protocol, sign-in and any tools of its own (MCP adds pb_ tools over the REST API). Replace it and the contract tools stay. A service (mcp.go).

title: mcp/v1
heading: Use
text: Add https:// /mcp to an MCP client and sign in. In Go, an extension adds a tool that isn't a contract operation, and tells agents what its tools are for: mcpv1.AddTool(app, mcpv1.Tool{ Name: "notes_summarize_week", Description: "Summarizes this week's notes.", ReadOnly: true, Call: func(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, args json.RawMessage) (any, error) { ... }, }) mcpv1.AddInstructions(app, "Use notes_summarize_week for weekly reviews.") mcpv1.Tools(app) lists what every provider serves.

title: mcp/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement mcpv1.Endpoint ( ServeMCP for requests to /mcp , Metadata for the protected resource metadata), provide it, and bind the routes once: mcpv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, myServer{}) mcpv1.Bind(app) Serve mcpv1.Tools(app) in tools/list and tools/call , calling each tool as the signed-in caller. /mcp skips PocketBase's pbRejectUnknownToken , so the provider rejects a bad token itself: a request with an Authorization header and no signed-in caller ( e.Auth is nil) gets 401 with a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token" challenge, never a guest's answer.

title: mcp/v1
heading: Extensions
text: mcp provides (default)

title: mcp/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: oauth/v1
text: An OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the app: authorization code with PKCE, device code, refresh, revocation, and client registration (dynamic, or by a client metadata document). The CLI's browser login and MCP clients such as Claude sign in through it, and get API tokens (tokens/v1). A routed contract (oauth.go): the OAuth specs fix its API's shape, so its provider serves it as it is.

title: oauth/v1
heading: Use
text: GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server the server's metadata (RFC 8414 puts it at the root) GET / POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/authorize sign in and consent (browser) POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/token codes and refresh tokens for access tokens POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device start a device-code sign-in GET / POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device/verify enter the device code (browser) POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/revoke revoke a token POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/register dynamic client registration (when on) GET / POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/provider/callback sign-in through an OAuth2 provider (Google, Apple, ...) In Go, another extension (MCP) turns on dynamic registration and sets token lifetimes: oauthv1.Contract.Of(app) → EnableDynamicRegistration() , SetAccessTTL(path, ttl) , Issuer(e) .

title: oauth/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement oauthv1.Server and serve the routes above ( extkit.EventServer or extkit.RouteBinder ); issue access tokens through tokens/v1.

title: oauth/v1
heading: Extensions
text: tokens provides mcp works with

title: oauth/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: remote/v1
text: Remote control of an app from afar: who your credential is and what the app offers, its status, a restart, and its log. Every client starts here: GET /api/_c/remote/v1 is the one fixed path, and its answer lists every other contract the app offers. Contracts that add an area (deploy/v1) require this one. A wire contract (remote.go); a multisite host can provide it for its instances, so it works for instances running stock PocketBase images.

title: remote/v1
heading: Use
text: Whoami GET /api/_c/remote/v1 public (the answer says more when you're signed in) Status GET /api/_c/remote/v1/status remote:read Restart POST /api/_c/remote/v1/restart remote Logs GET /api/_c/remote/v1/logs?n=100 (server-sent events) remote:read CLI: pocketone remote whoami status restart logs . Go: remotev1.Contract.Must(app) in the app, or remotev1.NewClient(url, token, http) from outside. The command-line client (linked remotes, saved logins, sign-in) is remoteclient. Hooks: remotev1.OnRestart(app) in Go, onRemoteRestart in pb_hooks , for every operation. MCP: a tool per operation ( remote_status , ...).

title: remote/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement remotev1.Remote and provide it in your extension's Register : remotev1.Contract.Provide(app, myRemote{}) A multisite host provides it for every instance with remotev1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(host, factory) and serves it with remotev1.W.HostHandler in its instance routes ( multisite.Host.InstanceRoutes , after the gates; see pocker and docker).

title: remote/v1
heading: Extensions
text: docker provides remotes provides (default) deploy requires

title: remote/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: restore/v1
text: Put an app's data back as it was at a moment. You ask for a moment ("Tuesday 15:00"); the app restores the closest point it has at or before it and tells you which one it used. Providers differ only in how close they get: pitr keeps continuous history: any second inside its window. backups, the default, uses PocketBase's own backups (local or S3): the latest backup made at or before the moment. It steps aside when pitr is on for the app. The app restarts to apply a restore; its data from before the restore is kept until the next one. A wire contract (restore.go); a multisite host may provide it for its instances (from host-level snapshots).

title: restore/v1
heading: Use
text: Points: what can be restored GET /api/_c/restore/v1 restore:read RestoreTo a moment POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore with {"at": " "} restore Points answers with the provider's name and either a window ( kind: "continuous" ) or a list of snapshots ( kind: "snapshots" , newest first), whether a restore is running, and the last restore. RestoreTo answers with the point it restores from; 422 no_point when there's nothing at or before the moment, 409 busy while another restore runs. Only superusers may call either. Dashboard: Settings → Backups gets a "Restore to a moment" section from this contract (ui/main.js), whichever extension provides it: a time picker over pitr's window, or one that says which backup a moment uses. Go: restorev1.Contract.Must(app).RestoreTo(ctx, auth, restorev1.RestoreInput{At: t}) , or restorev1.NewClient(url, token, http) from outside. Hooks: restorev1.OnRestoreTo(app, fn) in Go, onRestoreRestoreTo in pb_hooks : refuse or log a restore. MCP: restore_points and restore_restore_to .

title: restore/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement restorev1.Restorer and provide it in your extension's Register ( ProvideDefault if a better provider should replace yours). Report the point you'll actually restore from, and restart the app to apply it.

title: restore/v1
heading: Extensions
text: pitr provides backups provides (default)

title: restore/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: runtime/v1
text: What runs a multisite host's instances: pocker in-process, docker in containers. A host can have several at once, in preference order: each instance runs on the one it names ( runtime: docker in its record), else the first that can serve it (by PocketBase version, for example). Having a multisite section makes the binary a host; the runtimes are this contract's providers. A host-scope service contract, many providers in order (runtime.go).

title: runtime/v1
heading: Use
text: Pick and order the runtimes in pocketone.yaml ; by default it's every linked runtime that's configured, in link order (docker needs its docker section): multisite: {} providers: runtime/v1: [pocker, docker] # pocker first; docker for what pocker can't serve

title: runtime/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement runtimev1.Runtime ( Name , Serves , ServeInstance , Ready ) and any optional hooks the host calls ( Prechecker , Syncer , Starter , Shutdowner , Statser ). Provide it in a host extension's RegisterHost , only when it's configured: runtimev1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myRuntime)

title: runtime/v1
heading: Extensions
text: docker provides pocker provides

title: runtime/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: settings/v1
text: The settings an app's own superusers change for its extensions (PITR's S3 bucket, Bulk Mail's sending limits), behind one API: list them, read one, save one, test one without saving. Each extension keeps its settings its own way and registers a section; the provider serves them all. Settings an operator sets for a whole host stay in pocketone.yaml . A wire contract (settings.go).

title: settings/v1
heading: Use
text: List GET /api/_c/settings/v1 settings:read Get GET /api/_c/settings/v1/get?extension=pitr settings:read Save POST /api/_c/settings/v1/save with {"extension": "pitr", "values": {...}} settings Test POST /api/_c/settings/v1/test with {"extension": "pitr", "values": {...}} settings Each extension's values are its own shape (see its README). Secrets come back empty with a flag that they're set; saving an empty secret keeps the saved one. Test answers {"ok": false, "message": ...} when the settings don't work. Only superusers may call any of them.

title: settings/v1
heading: Provide
text: An extension with settings registers a section in its Register : settingsv1.Add(app, mySection{}) // Info, Get, Save; Test too if the settings can be checked and declares WorksWith: extkit.IDs("settings/v1") . A provider of the API (ext/settings by default) implements settingsv1.Settings over settingsv1.Sections(app) .

title: settings/v1
heading: Extensions
text: settings provides (default) bulkmail works with mailrelay works with pitr works with

title: settings/v1
heading: License

title: tls/v1
text: The TLS of a multisite host's main listener. Its provider hands the host a tls.Config (certificates on demand, for hostnames an instance serves) and, for HTTP challenges, a wrapper for the plain-HTTP listener. With no provider the host uses the certificate files in its server section, or plain HTTP. A host-scope service contract, one provider (tls.go).

title: tls/v1
heading: Use
text: Nothing to call: the host's listener uses it. Turn the provider on in its own section ( autotls: { auto: true } ).

title: tls/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement tlsv1.Provider and provide it in a host extension's RegisterHost ; only issue certificates for hostnames served reports true for. tlsv1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myTLS)

title: tls/v1
heading: Extensions
text: autotls provides

title: tls/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: tokens/v1
text: An app's API tokens, as other extensions use them. Tokens are scoped: a token limited to scopes works only on the requests those scopes reach. Extensions register their own scopes, read the token a request came with, and limit requests they make on someone's behalf, all through this package. A service with its own API (tokens.go), served at /api/_c/tokens/v1 .

title: tokens/v1
heading: Use
text: GET /api/_c/tokens/v1/scopes the scopes a token may hold, and who may own tokens GET /api/_c/tokens/v1 your tokens (superusers: ?owner= , ?ownerCollection= ) POST /api/_c/tokens/v1 create one ( {name, scopes, expires\ ttl} ); the secret is shown once DELETE /api/_c/tokens/v1/{id} revoke one POST /api/_c/tokens/v1/revoke-all revoke all of yours In Go: if tk, ok := tokensv1.Contract.Of(app); ok { tk.RegisterScope(tokensv1.Scope{Name: "notes:write", Description: "Change notes", Paths: []string{"/api/collections/notes/records"}, Methods: []string{"POST", "PATCH", "DELETE"}}) } g := tokensv1.FromRequest(e) // the request's token, or nil (a JWT, or none) ctx = tokensv1.WithScopes(ctx, []string{"notes:read"}) // requests made with ctx count as limited to these scopes

title: tokens/v1
heading: Provide
text: Implement tokensv1.Issuer ( Verify , RegisterScope , Scopes , Reaches ), authenticate requests that carry a token (setting tokensv1.RequestKey to the Grant ), honour WithScopes limits, and serve the token API (the provider binds its own routes, extkit.RouteBinder ).

title: tokens/v1
heading: Extensions
text: tokens provides deploy works with mcp works with remotes works with

title: tokens/v1
heading: License
text: MIT

title: Auto TLS
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree Automatic HTTPS certificates through ACME, with CertMagic (Caddy's certificate engine). PocketBase already gets Let's Encrypt certificates for serve example.com . Auto TLS takes over that job and adds other certificate authorities, extra domains and wildcard certificates. Status: stable on a multisite host, beta on a single app. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Auto TLS
heading: Install
text: Auto TLS is built into pocketone and off by default . Turn it on with --autotls (or auto: true in pocketone.yaml ). It only does something when the app serves HTTPS, that is with serve or --https ; on plain HTTP it stays idle, and without it PocketBase's own certificates are used as before. In your own Go build, register it before the app starts: import ( "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/autotls" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit" ) app := pocketbase.New() extkit.MustRegister(app, autotls.NewApp(autotls.Config{Auto: true, Email: "ops@example.com"})) app.Start()

title: Auto TLS
heading: Command-line flags
text: pocketone serve example.com --autotls --autotlsEmail ops@example.com pocketone serve example.com --autotls --autotlsDomains " .example.com" --autotlsDNS cloudflare # token in $CF_API_TOKEN --autotls false Turn it on. --autotlsEmail ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. --autotlsCA letsencrypt letsencrypt , letsencrypt-staging , zerossl , or an ACME directory URL. --autotlsDomains Extra domains, obtained at start (comma separated). Wildcards need --autotlsDNS . --autotlsDNS DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges. Only cloudflare is supported. --autotlsDNSTokenEnv CF_API_TOKEN Environment variable holding the DNS provider's API token.

title: Auto TLS
heading: pocketone.yaml
text: The autotls section sets the defaults for those flags. Flags win over the file. autotls: auto: true email: ops@example.com ca: letsencrypt domains: [" .example.com"] # wildcards need dns dns: provider: cloudflare api_token: $CF_API_TOKEN # read from the .env beside pocketone.yaml storage is only in the file: where certificates are kept (default pb_data/.autotls ). The DNS token can be given as api_token (write $VAR to read it from the .env beside the file) or through api_token_env , the name of an environment variable. api_token is only used when --autotlsDNS names the same provider as the file. The Cloudflare token needs permission to edit the zone's DNS. There are no dashboard settings.

title: Auto TLS
heading: autotls:
text: Automatic HTTPS certificates (ACME): auto, email, CA, domains, DNS-01, certificate storage. The --autotls flags win. auto bool Get certificates through ACME (CertMagic). Flag: --autotls. email string ACME account email, for expiry notices from the CA. Flag: --autotlsEmail. ca string letsencrypt (default), letsencrypt-staging, zerossl, or an ACME directory URL. Flag: --autotlsCA. storage string Where certificates are kept. Default pb_data/.autotls. domains list of string Extra domains to get at start; wildcards ( .example.com) need dns. Flag: --autotlsDomains. dns.provider string DNS provider for DNS-01 challenges (needed for wildcards): cloudflare. Flag: --autotlsDNS. dns.api_token string The provider's API token. Write $VAR to read it from the .env beside the file. dns.api_token_env string Or: the environment variable holding the token. Default CF_API_TOKEN. Flag: --autotlsDNSTokenEnv.

title: Auto TLS
heading: Use
text: Once on, there's nothing to click. Start the app as usual with serve (or --https ): Which hostnames get a certificate. The domains given to serve and their www. variants, issued on the first request for each, plus --autotlsDomains , obtained at start. Any other hostname is refused at the TLS handshake, so a random Host can't trigger issuance. How they're proved. TLS-ALPN-01 on the HTTPS port, or DNS-01 when a DNS provider is set (needed for wildcards). HTTP-01 isn't used on a single app, because port 80 is PocketBase's redirect server. Renewal is automatic. Where they're stored. pb_data/.autotls by default, separate from PocketBase's own .autocert_cache . Settings are checked at start, before anything touches the network. A wildcard domain without a DNS provider, a Cloudflare provider without a token, or an unknown provider stops the app with an error such as: tls.domains: wildcard " .example.com" needs a DNS provider (tls.dns); per-hostname certificates work without one With debug logging, the start shows autotls: CertMagic serves HTTPS certificates with the CA and extra domains. Use --autotlsCA letsencrypt-staging while testing, so failed attempts don't count against Let's Encrypt's rate limits.

title: Auto TLS
heading: Multisite hosts
text: On a multisite host (any runtime: pocker or docker), the stock pocketone binary runs autotls.New() , a host extension that gets certificates for every instance the host serves. It's configured by the same autotls section: autotls: auto: true email: ops@example.com storage: ./pb_root/.pocker-certs # default: .pocker-certs in the runtime's instance root domains: [" .example.com", "example.com"] dns: { provider: cloudflare, api_token_env: CF_API_TOKEN } # only needed for wildcards Without dns , every hostname the instance source maps gets its own certificate on its first TLS handshake, with any DNS host and no API token. Hostnames no instance serves never trigger issuance. Challenges include HTTP-01 on the host's port 80, as well as TLS-ALPN-01 and DNS-01. Certificate files ( server.tls.cert / key ) stay a core host feature. Setting both files and auto is an error. Certificates belong to the host, not to instances; the single-app extension ( NewApp ) is a separate type so it never runs per instance.

title: Auto TLS
heading: Building on Auto TLS
text: autotls.New() is a host extension ( multisite.Extension ) that provides the tls/v1 contract when auto is on. A host adds it to its host extensions (a pocker.Server built by hand takes it in Extensions too): h, err := multisite.FromConfig(multisite.Options{Extensions: []multisite.Extension{autotls.New()}}) AutoTLS.Config can be set in Go before the server starts; the autotls section is read only when Auto is false there. autotls.SupportedDNSProviders lists the dns.provider values it understands.

title: Auto TLS
heading: Example
text: Auto TLS is built into pocketone : examples/pocketone/main.go registers it with the other default extensions.

title: Auto TLS
heading: How it works
text: Go module github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/autotls . On a single app, an OnServe hook swaps the TLS config of PocketBase's HTTPS server for CertMagic's. PocketBase's own host policy (the serve domains and www. ) decides which on-demand hostnames are allowed. The certificate manager stops when the app terminates. TLS 1.2 is the minimum; h2 and http/1.1 are offered, and acme-tls/1 stays on for TLS-ALPN challenges. A wildcard in domains covers one level ( .example.com covers a.example.com , not a.b.example.com ).
