title: PocketPages v1 specification
text: The contract for ext/pages , PocketOne's server-rendered multi-page app extension. The test fixtures ( fixtures/ ), the starter kits and the PocketPages site are written against this document. Where the implementation and this document disagree, one of them is a bug. v1 is a clean API. It keeps PocketPages' ideas (a folder of files that become routes, EJS, layouts, middleware, private partials) and changes the shapes. Apps written for the npm package (0.x) don't run unchanged; "Changes from 0.x" (section 12) lists every difference.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 1. The pb_pages folder
text: Pages live in their own folder next to PocketBase's others: myapp/ pb_data/ pb_hooks/ pb_migrations/ pb_public/ pb_pages/ A single app finds it at pb_pages next to pb_data , or at --pagesDir (a relative path resolves against the working directory, like --hooksDir ). Serving is automatic: the standard PocketOne binary includes pages, and an app serves its pb_pages whenever the folder exists (it starts serving if the folder appears later). There is no on/off switch; no folder, no pages. Under the multitenant host every instance has its own pb_pages . If the folder doesn't exist, the extension does nothing for that app. Page code can require() modules from pb_pages ( _private/ folders, then node_modules ), then from the app's usual module paths. The same require works in modules, JSX/TSX components and EJS templates: ./x and ../x are files in pb_pages , relative to the requiring file, never above pb_pages . Without an extension, .js , .ts , .tsx , .jsx , .json and .cjs are tried, then a folder's package.json or index . A bare name ( pkg , pkg/sub , @scope/pkg ) is looked up first in _private/ folders, from the requiring file's folder up to the top of pb_pages , the same lookup as include (4.2; the extensions above are tried). Then it's looked up in the nearest node_modules folder, the same way up. A package resolves through its package.json : exports (a string, or conditions, where require , then node , then default are used), else main , else index.js . With exports , only what it lists can be required, and no entry may point outside the package. Then pb_hooks/node_modules , then the app folder's node_modules (the folder that holds pb_pages , where 0.x sites keep package.json ). Anything not found that way goes to the app's own module loader. If that fails too, the error lists the folders searched. A require cycle ( a requires b , which requires a ) gets the exports as they are so far, as in Node. node_modules is never routed or served, and isn't watched: after changing files in it, change any file in pb_pages (or restart) to reload. Page code runs in the app's JS VM, so PocketBase's JSVM globals ( $app , Record , $dbx , $security , ...) are available, as far as the sandbox allows for untrusted apps. Deploying: pb_pages is part of an app's code, next to pb_hooks and pb_migrations (the deploy extension uploads it the same way). Pages' own file access (routes, static files, includes, assets) never leaves pb_pages .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 1.1 Special names
text: A path segment (file or folder name) starting with one of these characters is never a URL: + Framework file: +config , +middleware , +page , +api ( .js or .ts ); +layout , +error , +404 ( .ejs , .jsx or .tsx ). +middleware , +page , +api and +layout : one of each per folder. +config , +error and +404 : only at the top of pb_pages (in a subfolder they're an error at startup). Any other + name is an error at startup. _ Private. _private/ folders hold partials and modules for include() and ctx.resolve() . Other _ names are ignored. - Ignored (drafts, notes). . Ignored (dotfiles), except a top-level .well-known/ , which is served as static files (ACME challenges, security.txt , app links). node_modules/ is never routed. Hook files ( .pb.js , .pb.ts ) belong in pb_hooks : in pb_pages they're a startup error and never served.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 1.2 Groups
text: A folder named (name) groups files without adding a URL segment: (marketing)/about.ejs serves /about . Groups can carry their own +layout.ejs , +middleware.js and _private/ .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 2.1 Pages
text: A page is a template file: .ejs , .md , .jsx or .tsx (4.5). index.ejs / about.ejs /about docs/index.md /docs (and /docs/ ) docs/routing.md /docs/routing products/[id].ejs /products/123 , with ctx.params.id = "123" [org]/[repo]/index.ejs /acme/web , with ctx.params = { org: "acme", repo: "web" } The extension is dropped. index maps to its folder. [name] matches exactly one non-empty segment. A segment may mix text and a parameter only as the whole segment; post-[id].ejs is an error at startup. A URL with a trailing slash matches the same route as without it. Pages never redirect to add or remove one. Matching is case-sensitive.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 2.2 API routes
text: A +api.js file serves its folder's URL without a template: feeds/rss/+api.js serves /feeds/rss . [param] folders work as for pages. If a folder has both +api.js and an index page, startup fails. A +page.js in a folder with no page (no template file) and no +api.js serves the folder's URL the same way, from JS: logout/+page.js serves /logout (3.2).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 2.3 Static files
text: Every other file is served as-is at its path (groups removed): assets/app.css serves /assets/app.css . Files that mustn't be served (build inputs such as a Tailwind source) take a - prefix: assets/-app.tailwind.css . Content type from the extension. ETag from the content hash; If-None-Match answers 304 . Fingerprinted URLs (see ctx.asset , 6.5) are served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 2.4 Precedence
text: /api/... and /_/... are PocketBase's. Pages never see them, and a pb_pages/api/ folder is an error at startup. Among matching routes the most specific wins: compare segment by segment from the left; a literal segment beats a [param] . So products/new.ejs beats products/[id].ejs for /products/new . A static file and a page can't claim the same URL (startup error). A URL nothing in pb_pages matches goes on to pb_public , then to PocketBase. If pb_pages/+404.ejs exists, a GET / HEAD that nothing (pages, pb_public , PocketBase) answers renders it inside the root layout with status 404 (never for /api/ or /_/ ). The root +middleware.js runs first; page code can still change the status. The route table is built when the app starts and rebuilt when anything in pb_pages changes. A rebuild never restarts the app or reloads pb_hooks . Startup errors (bad names, conflicts) are logged with the file path; the previous table keeps serving if there was one.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 3. Request flow
text: For a URL that matches a page or API route, one JS call does all of this, in order: Plugins: every plugin's extendContext , then every plugin's onRequest (built-in and JS plugins, in config order), so an onRequest can use what any plugin added to ctx . Middleware , root first: every +middleware.js from pb_pages/ down to the route's folder (groups included). Handlers : the folder's +page.js (or +api.js ): load , then the handler for the request method. Template (pages only), then layouts , innermost first. Response. The call runs under the app's usual JS limits (execution time, memory), as one unit. If any step sends a response ( ctx.res.redirect , json , html , text , file , sse ), the later steps are skipped.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 3.1 Middleware
text: // pb_pages/admin/+middleware.js module.exports = (ctx, next) = { if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login') ctx.data.section = 'admin' return next() } One signature: (ctx, next) . Call next() to continue; return its result. Returning without calling next() ends the request. If no response was sent, that's an error (500, and in dev the error page names the middleware file). Share data through ctx.data .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 3.2 Handlers: +page.js
text: // pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.js module.exports = { load(ctx) { ctx.data.product = ctx.app.findRecordById('products', ctx.params.id) }, post(ctx) { const { qty } = ctx.req.body() // ... return ctx.res.redirect( /products/${ctx.params.id} , { flash: 'Added to cart' }) }, } Exports any of load , get , post , put , patch , delete . All are optional: a page renders for any method. load runs for every method; then the method's handler, if there is one. HEAD runs load and get like GET (only the body is dropped), so keep side effects in post / put / patch / delete . A handler may set ctx.data fields, or return a plain object, which is shallow-assigned into ctx.data ( Object.assign ). There is no deep merge. A +page.js applies to every page in its folder. ctx.route.name tells them apart. A method with no handler still renders the page, for every method (like PHP): a template can handle a form itself by checking ctx.req.method , with no +page.js . Only routes with nothing to render ( +api.js , and a +page.js without a page) answer 405 for a method with no handler, with an Allow header listing the methods that have handlers ( GET, HEAD when there's a get ), in the order GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE . Without a page. A +page.js in a folder with no template serves the folder's URL from JS (2.2): there's nothing to render, so a handler must send a response ( ctx.res.html , ctx.res.redirect , ctx.res.json , ...), and returning without one is a 500. Methods without a handler answer 405 , GET included. Unlike +api.js , errors are pages ( +error.ejs or the HTML error page), not JSON. Folder middleware runs; layouts don't.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 3.3 API handlers: +api.js
text: Same exports as +page.js . There is no template, so a handler must send a response; returning without one is a // pb_pages/feeds/latest/+api.js module.exports = { get(ctx) { const posts = ctx.app.findRecordsByFilter('posts', 'published = true', '-created', 20) return ctx.res.json(posts.map((p) = ({ id: p.id, title: p.getString('title') }))) }, }

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.1 EJS
text: Run JS, no output Output, HTML-escaped Output, raw Nothing Also remove the newline right after the tag Also remove whitespace before / after the tag on its line script server code Same as Escaping replaces & " ' with & < > " ' . null and undefined output as an empty string. A template is compiled once per content hash and reused. In scope inside a template: ctx , data (= ctx.data ), params (= ctx.params ), include , slot , asset (= ctx.asset ), meta (= ctx.meta ), require (the same require as page code, 1). A template returns its text. There is no echo ; anything you want in the output goes through a tag.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.2 Partials: include
text: include(name, locals?) renders a template from a _private/ folder and returns its text. Use . A page or layout gets an empty locals . Including more than 32 levels deep is an error (recursion guard).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.3 Slots and layouts
text: +layout.ejs files wrap pages. A page's layouts are every +layout.ejs from its own folder up to pb_pages/ , applied innermost first. A folder may have one layout. { % slot(name, fn) defines a named slot: fn 's output is captured and nothing is output in place. slot(name) returns a slot's content ( '' if not defined). slot() returns the content being wrapped: the page, or the inner layout. (no call, as 0.x layouts wrote it) prints the same thing. Named slots defined by the page or by any inner layout are visible to every outer layout. Defining the same name again replaces it; inside the new definition's fn , slot(name) still returns the previous content, so a layout can wrap it ( slot('title', () = { % Docs: <% }) ). Layouts are skipped when the response isn't HTML (a handler set another Content-Type ) or after ctx.res.layout(false) . A page with an inner extension gets that type: robots.txt.ejs serves /robots.txt as text/plain and feed.xml.ejs serves /feed.xml as XML, so layouts are skipped. .html (or no inner extension) is HTML. Page code can still set another Content-Type .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.4 Markdown pages
text: A .md page is EJS first, then Markdown (CommonMark + GFM tables, strikethrough, task lists, autolinks). Front matter between lines at the top is YAML, removed before EJS runs. Each top-level key is passed to ctx.meta(key, value) , for pages and for included .md partials. Headings get id s: lowercased, characters other than a-z 0-9 - _ space removed, spaces to - ; a repeated id gets -1 , -2 , ... appended. Fenced code blocks render as " . Raw HTML passes through unchanged. Relative image paths go through ctx.asset . A .md partial is rendered (EJS, then Markdown) on its own and inserted as HTML; Markdown never runs twice on the same text. Leave blank lines around an include in Markdown so the HTML stays a block.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 4.5 JSX and TSX
text: .jsx and .tsx files are templates too: pages, layouts ( +layout.tsx ), +error / +404 , and partials in _private/ . They're compiled when first used by esbuild, which is built into the binary (no Node, no build step), and cached by content like EJS. TypeScript types are stripped, not checked. // pb_pages/products/[id].tsx import Price from './_private/Price' export default function Product({ data, slot }: any) { slot('title', data.product.getString('name')) return ( {data.product.getString('name')} ) } The file's default export is a component: a function from props to markup. Props: ctx , data , params , meta , asset , include , slot , children , plus an include 's locals. JSX renders straight to HTML on the server. There's no virtual DOM, no hydration, no client-side React. Event handler props (functions) are dropped; use plain attributes ( onclick="..." , hx-get , data-on:click ). Text and attribute values are escaped. dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html }} inserts raw HTML. class and className both work, as do for and htmlFor . style takes a string or an object ( { marginTop: 4 } → margin-top:4 ). true renders a bare attribute; false , null and undefined leave it out. renders with in front of it (JSX can't write a doctype). In a layout, children is the inner content. slot(name) reads a named slot, slot(name, content) sets one (content is JSX or a string), slot() is the same as children . include(name, locals) returns the partial's HTML, ready to put in JSX. EJS can include a .jsx / .tsx partial: its locals become props. Components are ordinary modules: import Card from './_private/Card' (resolved like require , 3.2). Partials are looked up with extensions in this order: .ejs , .md , .jsx , .tsx . TypeScript modules. +page.ts , +api.ts , +middleware.ts , +config.ts and any .ts file reached by require / import work like their .js versions. A module whose only export is export default behaves like module.exports = ... .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 5. Responses
text: A handler or middleware sent one That one Page rendered 200 text/html; charset=utf-8 (or the status set with ctx.res.status ) HEAD As GET , without a body No handler for the method Page: rendered as usual. +api.js or a +page.js without a page: 405 + Allow Error thrown 500 (see 8) JSON is only sent through ctx.res.json (or +api.js ). Template output is never parsed as JSON.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6. The ctx object
text: One object per request, passed to middleware, handlers, templates and plugins.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.1 ctx.req
text: method "GET" , "POST" , ... url { href, origin, pathname, search } query(name) First value of a query parameter as a string, or undefined query(name, { all: true }) Every value, as an array of strings query() { name: firstValue } for every parameter header(name) Request header, '' if absent cookie(name) Cookie value as a string, or undefined cookie(name, { json: true }) Cookie parsed as JSON ( undefined if absent or not JSON) cookies() { name: value } , strings body() Parsed body: JSON object, or form fields ( application/x-www-form-urlencoded , multipart/form-data ) as { name: value } (repeated names as arrays) files(name) Uploaded files for a multipart field, as PocketBase filesystem.File values ready for a record field ip Client IP as PocketBase resolves it (trusted proxy settings apply) event The underlying PocketBase RequestEvent , for anything not covered here Query values and cookies are strings unless you ask for JSON. Nothing is parsed for you.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.2 ctx.res
text: status(code) Status for the rendered page. Returns ctx.res . header(name, value) Set a response header; returns ctx.res . header(name) reads it back. cookie(name, value, options?) Set a cookie. Non-string values are JSON.stringify 'd; the value is then percent-encoded ( encodeURIComponent ), and ctx.req.cookie decodes it. Defaults: path=/ , HttpOnly , SameSite=Lax , Secure when the request is HTTPS. Options: path , domain , maxAge (seconds), expires (a Date , milliseconds since the epoch, or a date string; with maxAge too, browsers use maxAge ), httpOnly , secure , sameSite . clearCookie(name, options?) Expire a cookie (same path / domain as when set). redirect(location, { status = 302, flash }?) or redirect(location, status) Send a redirect. status must be a 3xx code. flash sets a one-time message (6.4). json(data) / json(status, data) Send JSON. html(html) / html(status, html) Send HTML as-is (no layouts). text(text) / text(status, text) Send plain text. file(path) Send a file from pb_pages (path relative to pb_pages ). sse() Start a text/event-stream response; returns { send(event, data, { id, retry }?), comment(text), close() } . layout(false) Render this page without layouts (e.g. an HTML fragment for htmx). sent true once a response has been sent.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.3 Data and routing
text: ctx.data Plain object shared by middleware, handlers and templates. Starts as {} . ctx.params Route parameters, strings. Never includes query parameters. ctx.route { path, name, file } : the URL pattern without groups ( /products/[id] , /docs for docs/index.md ), the file name without extension ( [id] , index ; +api for API routes) and the file relative to pb_pages , groups included.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.4 Flash messages
text: ctx.res.redirect(path, { flash: 'Saved' }) stores the message as JSON in a cookie ( pp_flash , encoded like any cookie, HttpOnly , Max-Age=300 ). ctx.flash() on the next request returns it and clears it ( Max-Age=0 ). It returns undefined when there is none. Calling it again in the same request returns the same value. A flash can be any JSON value.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 6.5 Helpers
text: ctx.auth The authenticated record, or null . Set by PocketBase's own auth (an Authorization header) or by the auth plugin's cookie. ctx.app The app ( $app ): records, collections, settings. ctx.pb() A PocketBase JS SDK client (the bundled synchronous build) acting as the signed-in user ( ctx.auth ), or as a guest. Its requests go to the app's own API in-process (no network), so collection API rules, expand and field visibility apply exactly as for a browser. API errors throw the SDK's ClientResponseError ( e.status , e.response ). Only /api/ routes; file uploads through the SDK aren't supported (use ctx.app ). ctx.env(name) Environment variable, '' if unset (the app's environment; under the sandbox, the instance's). ctx.log debug , info , warn , error : to the app's log. debug only shows in dev. ctx.meta(key, value?) Per-request key/value store for page metadata (title, description). Set with two arguments, read with one. ctx.asset(path) URL for a static file in pb_pages , with its content hash: asset('app.css') → /assets/app.3f9a1c2b7d4e.css . Relative paths resolve from the current file's folder; / -paths from pb_pages . A path that isn't a file in pb_pages is returned unchanged. ctx.include(name, locals?) Render a _private/ partial from JS (handlers, middleware, plugins) and get its text; same lookup as the template include , from the route's folder. ctx.resolve(name, { mode }?) Load a module from _private/ , looked up from the route's folder up (like ctx.include ; wherever it's called from); without an extension, the name, then .js , .ts and .json are tried. Modes: require (default, the module's exports), raw (file text), script (text wrapped in ), style (wrapped in ). ctx.pagesDir The absolute path of this app's pb_pages folder, e.g. for listing files with $os.readDir . Read-only. ctx.store(name, value?) The app's in-memory store ( $app.store() ): set with two arguments, read with one. ctx.dev true in dev mode. Fingerprinted asset names carry the first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256: name. .ext .

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 7. Configuration: +config.js
text: // pb_pages/+config.js module.exports = { plugins: ['auth', 'realtime', 'datastar'], debug: false, } plugins [] Module names, built-in names ( auth , realtime ), or JS plugin factories such as add-ons (9). EJS and Markdown are always on. debug false Detailed error pages and ctx.log.debug output even outside dev mode. A string in plugins is a module name, required from +config.js (1): a _private/ file ( 'datastar' finds _private/datastar.js ), a package in node_modules ( 'my-plugin' ) or a path ( './plugins/my-plugin.js' ). Its export, or its default export, must be a plugin factory (9.2). Only when no module by that name is found is the string a built-in (9.1), so a _private/auth.js or a package named auth would replace the built-in auth . To skip that order and load one exact file, list require('./path') instead of the name: a ./ path is never looked up in _private/ or node_modules . A module that is found but fails to load is an error; it never falls back to the built-in. +config.js runs on each page request, so these aren't caught at startup: unknown keys, names that are neither a module nor a built-in, or a plugin listed twice make every page answer with an error (a 500; dev mode shows the reason on the page), and the reason goes to the log.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 8. Errors
text: Anything thrown in middleware, a handler or a template becomes a 500 . Dev mode or debug: true : an HTML error page with the message, the file and line (template lines map to the .ejs / .md source), and the stack trimmed to pb_pages -relative paths. Otherwise: a plain "Something went wrong" page. The full error always goes to the app's log. throw ctx.httpError(status, message) sends that status (e.g. 404 , 403 ) with a plain page showing message . In a +api.js it's JSON: { "status": 404, "message": "..." } . A custom error page: pb_pages/+error.ejs renders for every ctx.httpError and every 500 outside dev mode, with ctx.error = { status, message } , inside the root layout.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 9.1 Built-in
text: Turned on by name in +config.js when no module by that name is found (7). auth : cookie sessions on PocketBase auth, without calling the app over HTTP. Every request: reads the pb_auth cookie, validates the token, sets ctx.auth (or clears a bad cookie). The cookie holds { token, record } as JSON (the JS SDK's cookie format), HttpOnly , SameSite=Lax , Secure on HTTPS, lasting as long as the collection's auth token. identity arguments accept any of the collection's identity fields (email by default). MFA: pages has no second sign-in step yet, so every sign-in method (password, OTP, anonymous, OAuth2, and register 's sign-in) refuses an account that needs MFA, as PocketBase decides it: the collection has MFA on and its MFA rule matches the record (an empty rule matches everyone; a rule that can't be checked counts as a match). The error says so; nothing is signed in and an OTP isn't used up. A wrong password still says only that the credentials are invalid. ctx.session.signIn(record) is the exception: it signs in a record the app authenticated itself. ctx.session.authMethods({ collection }) → { password: { enabled, identityFields }, otp: { enabled }, mfa: { enabled }, oauth2: { enabled, providers: [{ name, displayName }] } } , as PocketBase's auth-methods API. ctx.session.register(email, password, { collection = 'users', data, verify = true, signIn = true }) : creates the record; sends the verification email when verify ; signs in when signIn . ctx.session.signInWithPassword(identity, password, { collection }) ctx.session.requestOTP(email, { collection, create = false }) → otpId . Always returns an id (unknown emails get one that never validates, as PocketBase does); with create: true a missing record is created first. ctx.session.signInWithOTP(otpId, code, { collection }) ctx.session.signInAnonymously({ collection }) ctx.session.requestOAuth2(provider, { collection, redirectPath = '/auth/oauth/confirm', redirect = true }) : stores state in a cookie and returns the provider's URL; with redirect it also sends the redirect ( ctx.res.sent ). redirectPath must be a path on this site. PKCE is used when the provider supports it. ctx.session.signInWithOAuth2(state, code, { createData }?) : completes it on the redirect path (the state cookie carries the provider, collection and PKCE verifier; it lasts 10 minutes and works once). The sign-in runs through PocketBase's own auth-with-oauth2 endpoint in-process, so sign-up, account linking (to the signed-in account, if any), the anti-hijacking checks and onRecordAuthWithOAuth2Request hooks behave as in PocketBase. createData is extra data for a new record. Returns { token, record, meta } ( meta is PocketBase's OAuth2 meta, with isNew ). Accounts that need MFA throw an error: pages doesn't do MFA yet. Apple answers with a POST, so read state and code from ctx.req.body() there. On HTTPS the state cookie is SameSite=None so it survives that cross-site POST. ctx.session.signIn(record) : set the cookie for a record you authenticated yourself. ctx.session.signOut() Email flows, with PocketBase's own checks and mail templates: requestVerification(email, { collection }) , confirmVerification(token) , requestPasswordReset(email, { collection }) , confirmPasswordReset(token, password, passwordConfirm) , requestEmailChange(newEmail) (needs ctx.auth ), confirmEmailChange(token, password) . Request methods never reveal whether an email exists. Every sign-in method sets ctx.auth for the rest of the request and returns { token, record } . realtime : PocketBase realtime from page code. ctx.realtime.send(topic, data, { filter }?) sends to every client subscribed to topic (the filter only narrows that set). data is always JSON-encoded (a string arrives as a JSON string, as PocketBase's own messages do). filter(client) returns true to include a client. client is PocketBase's realtime client: id() , get(key) , set(key, value) , hasSubscription(topic) . ctx.realtime.client(id) returns one client by id, or null . Sending never waits for slow clients: each message is handed to the client's queue in the background.

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 9.2 JS plugins
text: A JS plugin is a factory that returns hooks: module.exports = (config) = ({ name: 'my-plugin', onRequest(ctx) {}, // before middleware extendContext(ctx) { ctx.hello = () = 'hi' }, transform({ html, ctx, file }) { return html }, // after each page or layout renders (not partials) }) config is the plugin's entry in +config.js when it's an object ( { factory, ...options } ), else {} . name is required and unique. 0.x hook names ( onExtendContextApi , onRender , onResponse , handles ) are an error that names the v1 hook to use. There's no hook for treating other kinds of files as pages: a page's inner extension already does that ( robots.txt.ejs serves /robots.txt as text/plain , 4.5). Hooks run in config order. Every hook is optional. JS plugins run with the same permissions as the rest of the app's JS (sandboxed in a multitenant host).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 9.3 Add-ons
text: Plugins for third-party libraries ship as JS files in ext/pages/addons/ , not built into ext/pages . Copy one into pb_pages/_private/ and list it in +config.js by name ( 'datastar' ). datastar.js (Datastar) adds ctx.datastar : ctx.datastar.scripts({ spa: { scope, selector }, realtime }?) returns the script tags ( spa turns on client-side navigation for links under scope , swapping selector ). With realtime: true the page subscribes to the datastar realtime topic and sets a $clientId signal to its realtime client id. ctx.datastar.patchElements(html, { selector, mode }?) , ctx.datastar.patchSignals(signals, { onlyIfMissing }?) ( signals is an object), ctx.datastar.executeScript(js) send SSE events on the current response. The first one starts the stream ( ctx.res.sent becomes true ); later steps still run, but their output isn't sent and the automatic patch below doesn't happen. The stream closes when the request ends. ctx.datastar.signals() returns the request's signals as an object (from the datastar query parameter on GET , the JSON body otherwise). readSignals(target) (or 0.x's readSignals(request, target) ) merges them into target and returns it. Script helpers, each an executeScript (options { eventId, retryDuration, autoRemove = true, attributes } ; autoRemove adds data-effect="el.remove()" so the script tag removes itself, attributes is a list of extra attribute strings such as 'type="module"' ): consoleLog(msg) , consoleError(err) , redirect(url) (a full page load), dispatchCustomEvent(name, detail, { selector, bubbles, cancelable, composed, eventId, retryDuration }?) (on document by default), replaceURL(url) ( history.replaceState ) and prefetch(urls) (a speculationrules script that stays in the page). mode is one of outer (default), inner , replace , prepend , append , before , after , remove . When a request has Datastar-Request: true , the rendered page (without layouts) is sent as a patchElements event, into Datastar-Selector if given. ctx.datastar.realtime.patchElements(html, options?, { filter }?) , .patchSignals(signals, options?, { filter }?) and .executeScript(js, { filter }?) send the same events to datastar realtime subscribers (needs realtime ).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 10. Dev mode
text: On when the app runs in dev mode ( --dev ) or +config.js sets debug: true : detailed error pages (8); ctx.log.debug output; template cache keyed by content hash, so edits show on the next request (the route table is rebuilt on any file change in every mode).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 11. Starter kits
text: pocketone pages create [--starter ] creates the folder (it must not exist) and copies the whole kit into it. Run it with cd && pocketone serve --dir ./pb_data ( pocketone keeps pb_data next to its executable by default; pb_pages and pb_migrations are found next to pb_data ). pocketone pages starters lists the kits. Kits: minimal (default), mvp , htmx , daisyui , daisyui-docs , datastar , auth . The command needs a build that includes ext/pages . It copies pb_pages/ plus anything beside it ( pb_migrations/ , README.md , a package.json for CSS tooling). Kits ship inside ext/pages ( starters/ ).

title: PocketPages v1 specification
heading: 12. Changes from 0.x (npm PocketPages)

EJS and Markdown always on Plugin hooks onRequest({ request, response }) , onExtendContextApi , onRender , onResponse , handles extendContext(ctx) , onRequest(ctx) , transform ; a 0.x hook name is an error .pb.js beside pages in pb_hooks/pages/ Hook files stay in pb_hooks ; in pb_pages they're a startup error require('../lib/x') could reach pb_hooks from the pages folder require never leaves pb_pages ; use require(__hooks + '/lib/x') Cookies (and pb_auth ) readable by browser JS HttpOnly by default; pass { httpOnly: false } for a cookie the page's JS reads. pb_auth stays HttpOnly , so pb.authStore.loadFromCookie(document.cookie) no longer works Realtime send(topic, message) sent the message as is; filter(clientId, client, topic, message) replaced the subscription check The data is JSON-encoded (a string arrives quoted: JSON.parse it); filter(client) narrows clients that are subscribed to the topic .md , .jsx , .tsx were static files unless a plugin handled them Always pages EJS ran over the whole .md file, front matter included Front matter is plain YAML, read before EJS runs auth plugin through the JS SDK over HTTP ( api.pb() ) ctx.session. , direct app calls url() , stringify() , micro-dash globals Removed: use ctx.req.url , JSON.stringify , plain JS pb() (js-sdk plugin over HTTP to localhost:8090 ) ctx.pb() : same SDK, built in, in-process, as the signed-in user Route with fewer segments could match a longer URL Segment counts must match create-pocketpages pocketone pages create [--starter ]

title: PITR
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree Point-in-time restore: your database as it was at any moment in the last few days, restored from the dashboard. History is recorded with Litestream, next to your data or in an S3-compatible bucket. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: PITR
heading: Install
text: PITR is built into pocketone and on by default . Every app it serves starts recording history the first time it serves; there's nothing to install. To run without it: pocketone serve --pitr=false In your own Go build, register it before the app starts: app := pocketbase.New() pitr.MustRegister(app, pitr.Config{}) app.Start()

title: PITR
heading: On, off and how far back
text: Set it in pocketone.yaml : pitr: enabled: true # false turns it off retention: 72h # how far back a restore can go snapshot_interval: 24h # how often a full copy is taken Or with flags, which win over the file: --pitr true Record history while serving. --pitr=false turns it off. --pitrRetention 72h How far back a restore can go. A shorter snapshot_interval makes restores faster and uses more storage.

title: PITR
heading: Where the history is stored
text: By default the history is kept next to your database, in pb_data/litestream/ . That protects you from mistakes in your data, but not from losing the disk. To keep it somewhere else, use your own S3-compatible bucket: Open Settings → Backups in the dashboard and find Point-in-time restore . Tick Store the history in my own S3 bucket and fill in the endpoint, bucket, region, access key and secret. Tick Force path-style addressing for MinIO and similar servers. The prefix defaults to litestream . Click Test connection to check that the bucket accepts a write, then Save . From then on the history is recorded in the bucket, starting with a fresh copy, so restores go back to the moment you saved. The secret is never shown again after saving. If the app runs with an encryption key ( --encryptionEnv ), the secret is stored encrypted.

title: PITR
heading: pitr:
text: Point-in-time restore: on by default, retention, snapshot interval. The --pitr and --pitrRetention flags win. enabled bool On unless false. The --pitr flag wins. retention duration How far back a restore can go. Default 72h. The --pitrRetention flag wins. snapshot_interval duration How often a full copy is taken. Default 24h. Shorter: faster restores, more storage.

title: PITR
heading: What's covered
text: Your database: records, collections, settings and superusers. Not uploaded files, pb_hooks , pb_public or the logs database. Use PocketBase's backups for those. History starts with the first change after PITR is turned on, and goes back as far as the retention allows (72 hours by default).

title: PITR
heading: Restore from the dashboard
text: Open Settings → Backups . Restore to a moment (the restore/v1 contract's section) shows how far back you can go; Point-in-time restore shows how big the history is and where it's stored. Under Restore to , pick a date and time, then click Restore . The app keeps serving while the old database is rebuilt, then restarts with it. Only superusers see this section.

title: PITR
heading: Undo a restore
text: The database you replaced is kept in pb_data/litestream/before-restore.db , and history keeps recording, so a restore can be undone. After a restore, the section shows when you restored and to what time, with an Undo this restore button.

title: PITR
heading: From the command line
text: pocketone pitr status pocketone pitr restore --at 2026-11-11T14:05:00Z --to /tmp/then.db # a copy, any time pocketone pitr restore --at 2026-11-11T14:05:00Z # in place --at takes an RFC 3339 time. With --to , you get a copy of the database as it was, to inspect or pull records from; the app keeps running. Without --to , run it while the server is stopped: the restore is swapped in when it next starts.

title: PITR
heading: What it costs
text: About 176 KiB of memory per serving app, and the storage for your history. Replication runs only while the app is serving, never during CLI commands.

title: PITR
heading: Works with
text: Pocker Every instance on the host gets PITR. The pitr section sets the defaults for all of them; each instance can override enabled and retention (below). A restore restarts only that instance, and sleeping instances cost nothing. S3 Fallback Mount litestream on a backend and every app without its own bucket keeps its history there, under its own prefix. An app's own bucket (Settings → Backups) still wins. Multitenant (planned) Sets each instance's enabled and retention from its plan, for example a plan without PITR. PocketBase backups pb_data/litestream/ is left out of backup zips, and restoring a zip doesn't wipe it.

title: PITR
heading: Per-instance settings (pocker)
text: Each instance can override enabled and retention in its extensions.pitr settings, from instances.yaml or a provider: instances: id: abc extensions: { pitr: { retention: 168h } } id: free-plan-app extensions: { pitr: { enabled: false } } Each instance's history goes to instances/ /litestream/ in the shared bucket, or its own pb_data/litestream/ . A bucket in an instance's settings is refused, so credentials never sit in instance data.

title: PITR
heading: Building on PITR
text: Store history somewhere else. PITR asks PocketBase for a filesystem of kind litestream ( pitr.Kind ) through OnFilesystemCreate . Answer it and the history goes to your filesystem; S3 Fallback works this way. Set it per instance. Write extensions.pitr.enabled and extensions.pitr.retention into an instance's settings; PITR reads them when the instance starts. Multitenant will work this way. Go API. ( pitr.Extension).Status(ctx, app) returns the restorable window, size, destination and last restore; Restore(ctx, app, at) restores an app to a time. restore/v1. PITR provides the restore/v1 contract (superusers): GET /api/_c/restore/v1 for the window, size, destination and last restore, POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore with {"at": " "} to restore. Without PITR the same calls restore the latest backup before the moment (Backups), so clients and agents don't care which is on.

title: PITR
heading: Example
text: example/main.go runs one app with point-in-time restore on, keeping three days. Run it with go run ./example serve from this folder. // Command example runs one PocketOne app with point-in-time restore: Litestream copies data.db continuously into // pb_data/litestream/, and Settings → Backups gets a "Point-in-time restore" section. // // go run ./example serve // go run ./example pitr status // go run ./example pitr restore --at 2026-11-11T14:05:00Z --to /tmp/then.db // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password. package main import ( "log" "time" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pitr" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" pitr.MustRegister(app, pitr.Config{ Retention: 72 time.Hour, // on by default; Enabled: false turns it off // Bucket: &pitr.Bucket{Endpoint: "...", Bucket: "...", Region: "auto", AccessKey: "...", Secret: "...", Label: "EU"}, }) if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: PITR
heading: How it works
text: Go module github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pitr , Litestream v0.5.18 (pinned). example/main.go runs one app with local history. Litestream continuously copies data.db to its destination: the app's own bucket (its PITR settings), else a filesystem of kind litestream (an OnFilesystemCreate handler, such as S3 Fallback), else pb_data/litestream/ . Buckets go through PocketBase's own S3 client, not the AWS SDK. Each LTX file's timestamp is kept in object metadata, so restoring to a time doesn't depend on upload times. Replication runs only while the app serves ( OnServe ), never for CLI commands. On terminate it's flushed and detached, so under pocker a sleeping instance costs nothing. A restore is built into a side file while the app keeps serving, then swapped in by app.Restart() . The replaced database is kept as pb_data/litestream/before-restore.db . Apps with different retention get separate Litestream stores, since Litestream applies retention per store. Cost per serving app: about 176 KiB of memory, 4 goroutines, 5 file descriptors. Binary: about +4 MiB.

text: MIT

title: Pocker
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree Many PocketOne instances in one process (like Docker, but for PocketOne), routed by hostname. Each instance is a normal app folder and starts on its first request, in tens of milliseconds. Pocker provides runtime/v1 for Multisite; its peer Docker runs each instance in a container instead. Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Pocker
heading: Install
text: Pocker is built into pocketone . Add a multisite section to pocketone.yaml and pocketone serve hosts many instances instead of one app, with pocker as the runtime (docker too, when it has its docker section): multisite: {} In your own Go build, add it to the host's extensions ( examples/pocketone/multi.go is the stock binary's version), or run a pocker.Server on its own as the example does: h, err := multisite.FromConfig(multisite.Options{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath, Extensions: []multisite.Extension{ &pocker.Provider{ Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath, Standard: standard.New(), // every instance gets the standard set (tokens, mcp, pitr, ...) Extensions: []pocker.Extension{ myextension.New(), // your own PocketOne extensions, on every instance too }, }, }}) The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pocker .

title: Pocker
heading: Configure
text: The pocker section sets where instances live, the JS pool, outbound network and the default limits for every instance (keys below). Listeners, instances and the firewall are the Multisite sections ( server , instances , firewall ). multisite: {} instances: { file: ./instances.yaml } pocker: root: ./pb_root # one folder per instance: / hooks_pool_size: 2 egress_allow: [] # private networks instances may still reach max_js_execution: 30s # default limits; each instance can override them max_js_allocation: 64MiB An instance overrides any limit in its own limits (missing fields keep the default): instances: id: shop hosts: [shop.example.com] limits: { max_js_execution: 60s, max_concurrent_js: 32 } Every instance runs the PocketOne code in the binary; an instance's version is ignored.

title: Pocker
heading: pocker:
text: Runtime provider pocker: instances run in-process (root folder, hooks pool, egress allow list, instance limit defaults). root string ./pb_root The folder holding one folder per instance: / . hooks_pool_size int 2 Ignored: each instance has one JS VM (ext/jsvm). Kept so existing configs load. max_js_execution duration 30s Longest any single JS call (hook, route, cron job, migration) may run. max_js_allocation int 67108864 Largest result a JS built-in may allocate in one step, such as 64MiB. max_call_stack_size int 2000 Deepest JS recursion allowed. max_sleep duration 10s Longest a JS sleep() call may wait. max_query_duration duration 30s Longest an SQL statement without its own deadline may run. http_send_max_timeout duration 1m0s Longest timeout a JS $http.send call may use. http_send_max_body int 10485760 Largest response body a JS $http.send call may read, such as 10MiB. max_concurrent_js int 16 JS calls an instance runs at once; more wait up to max_js_execution, then fail. egress_allow list of string Private networks (CIDRs) instances may still connect to. Default none: public addresses only.

title: Pocker
heading: Try it with any hostname
text: # pocketone.yaml server: { http: "127.0.0.1:8090" } multisite: {} instances: { dev: true } pocker: { root: ./pb_root } pocketone serve curl -H 'Host: blog.localhost' http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/health # creates and serves ./pb_root/blog.localhost In dev mode a hostname no instance maps becomes an instance named after it, its folder is made on first use, and it runs in dev mode. In production only the hostnames in the instances file are served (see Multisite).

title: Pocker
heading: Each instance
text: A normal app folder, / : pb_data , pb_hooks , pb_migrations , pb_public . Its dashboard is at https:// /_/ . Its JS hooks see only its own secrets , through $os.getenv and process.env . A change to its secrets , encryption_key , access , limits , dev , dir , superusers , private , extensions or remote restarts its app on the next request, after in-flight requests finish. A hostname change doesn't restart it. A change in pb_hooks restarts just that instance. A broken hooks file affects only that instance (below).

title: Pocker
heading: Broken hook files
text: In dev mode, a pb_hooks file that fails to load is logged and skipped, and the rest of the instance runs, so you can fix it live. Otherwise an instance doesn't start with a broken file. When a running instance's pb_hooks change, the new code starts beside the running app and takes over only once it has started. If it fails to load, the previous code keeps serving and the error goes to the instance log, so a bad edit never takes a working instance down.

title: Pocker
heading: Logs
text: The app's own logs (the dashboard's Logs) are per instance, in its pb_data . console. from JS hooks goes to /logs/exec.log as JSON lines ( message , stream , time ), rotated to exec.log.1 at 10 MiB. A start failure is written there too.

title: Pocker
heading: Works with
text: Multisite Routing, listeners, instances file and gates. Pocker is one of its runtimes (runtime/v1). Sandbox Every instance's JS hooks, SQL and outbound network run in it, so one instance can't reach another or the host. Firewall Peer allow-list and rate limits in front of every instance; per-instance limits in extensions.firewall . Auto TLS In the stock binary: certificates for the hostnames instances map ( autotls section). Server Timing In the stock binary: Server-Timing headers on every response. Mailtrap In the stock binary: dev instances with SMTP off send mail to a local inbox. Edge Instances another edge runs are forwarded there instead of started here. Stats Measures disk use and last request for each instance under root . PocketOne extensions In your own build, any extension such as PITR, S3 Fallback or Mail Relay runs on every instance, and an instance's extensions. settings override the extension's defaults. enabled: false turns it off for that instance.

title: Pocker
heading: Building on Pocker
text: Standard set (required). pocker.Provider.Standard (or pocker.Server.Standard , ManagerOptions.Standard ) is ext/standard's set, and Pocker won't start an instance without it: a server without one refuses to run, so no host can make an instance that lacks the standard extensions. Every instance gets its members, each turned off per instance with extensions. .enabled: false , and its startup lines ( standard: on: ... ) are in the instance's own log. Listing a member in Extensions too is an error. Contracts the host provides. Server.Host (or Provider.Host ) is the host's contract scope. A contract the host provides for its instances steps aside inside each instance's app, and the host answers it on the instance's hostname in Server.InstanceRoutes (or Provider.InstanceRoutes , ManagerOptions.InstanceRoutes ): after the gates and the blocked answer, before the app. pocker.Remote(m, host) is remote/v1 for Pocker instances (restart through the Manager, logs from logs/exec.log ); add your own auth: host := extkit.NewScope("multisite") srv.Host = host srv.OnStart = func(m pocker.Manager) { remotev1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(host, pocker.Remote(m, host)) } srv.InstanceRoutes = append(srv.InstanceRoutes, func(next http.Handler) http.Handler { return remotev1.W.HostHandler(host, multisite.InstanceID, myAuth, next) }) deploy/v1 works the same way with deploy.New(...) as the handler: deployv1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(host, ...) and extkit.HostRoutes(host, deployv1.Contract, multisite.InstanceID, next) as an instance route. Extensions. pocker.Provider.Extensions (or pocker.Server.Extensions ) takes any extkit.Extension , registered on each instance's app before it starts with that instance's extensions. settings. Host-level code can implement AppIniter , JSIniter , Starter , or be a host extension ( multisite.Extension , registered on the host like any other: servertiming, autotls). See POCKER.md. Setup per instance. SetupApp(inst, app) runs after migrations and before the app serves, e.g. to add a route checked against inst.Private . Manager. OnStart hands host code the Manager : WithInstanceStopped(ctx, id, fn) changes an instance's files while it's stopped (deploys, restores), StartInstance , Running , InstanceDir , LogInstance . Restarts. app.Restart() (a backup restore, PITR) restarts only that instance.

title: Pocker
heading: Example
text: A Pocker build with one extension: a Go route and an admin dashboard page on every instance, in dev mode. Run it from this folder with go run ./example , then open http://blog.localhost:8090/_/ (login admin@example.com / password ). // Command pocker-extension is a Pocker build with one extension: a Go route and an admin dashboard page, // added to every instance. See docs/extensions.md. // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password. package main import ( "context" "embed" "io/fs" "log" "net/http" "os" "os/signal" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/apis" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pocker" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/standard" ) //go:embed ui var uiFiles embed.FS func main() { cfg := pocker.DefaultConfig() cfg.Dev = true // any hostname; drop this for production (instances.yaml required) ui, _ := fs.Sub(uiFiles, "ui") srv := &pocker.Server{ Config: cfg, Standard: standard.New(), // every instance gets the standard extensions (tokens, mcp, pages, pitr, ...) // Runs for every instance's app after its migrations, before it serves. SetupApp: func(inst pocker.Instance, app core.App) error { // local testing: every instance gets superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" if err := devusers.Ensure(app); err != nil { return err } app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se core.ServeEvent) error { // a Go route, superuser only se.Router.GET("/api/hello", func(e core.RequestEvent) error { return e.JSON(http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"instance": inst.ID}) }).Bind(apis.RequireSuperuserAuth()) // an admin dashboard extension: ui/main.js is loaded by the dashboard before its router starts se.UIExtensions = append(se.UIExtensions, core.UIExtension{Name: "hello", FS: ui}) return se.Next() }) return nil }, } ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt) defer stop() if err := srv.Run(ctx); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }

title: Pocker
heading: Untrusted instances
text: Pocker runs every instance's JS hooks in the sandbox. For why that's safe enough to host code from people you don't know, and where it isn't, see How is this safe?. Memory is the main limit: only one-shot allocations are capped, so a hook that grows memory slowly affects the whole process. POCKER.md lists what the sandbox covers.

title: Pocker
heading: Reference
text: POCKER.md is the full guide: production pocketone.yaml , every instance field, extension interfaces, the sandbox, PocketBase changes and versions.

title: Pocker
heading: License
text: MIT

title: Pocker
text: Pocker hosts many PocketOne instances in one process. It is PocketOne itself (this repo tracks upstream PocketBase and shares its history) plus a small engine in this folder, run by the stock pocketone binary as a runtime/v1 provider (a multisite section in pocketone.yaml). One port, many instances. Each request's hostname maps to a canonical instance id. Each instance is a normal app folder, / ( pb_data , pb_hooks , pb_migrations , pb_public ), with its own environment for JS hooks ( $os.getenv , process.env ), its own JS migrations and its own settings encryption key. An instance's app starts on its first request (tens of milliseconds) and keeps running.

title: Pocker
heading: Dev mode: any hostname
text: # pocketone.yaml server: { http: "127.0.0.1:8090" } multisite: {} instances: { dev: true } pocker: { root: ./pb_root } pocketone serve curl -H 'Host: blog.localhost' http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/health # creates and serves ./pb_root/blog.localhost A hostname the instance source doesn't map uses the hostname itself as its id (lowercase, no port, no trailing dot; anything that isn't a safe folder name gets 400), its folder is created on first use, and apps run in dev mode. The instances file (or another source) is optional in dev mode; hosts it maps keep their own ids.

title: Pocker
heading: Production: mapped hostnames only
text: Without dev mode, Pocker serves only what an instance source maps. The built-in source is the instances section's YAML file (reloaded when it changes; the host refuses to start without it): # instances.yaml instances: id: blog # folder /blog hosts: [blog.example.com, www.blog.example.com] id: shop hosts: [shop.example.com] secrets: { STRIPE_KEY: sk_live_... } # the app's environment encryption_key: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef # encrypts the app's stored settings; not visible to JS access: { cors_origins: [https://shop.example.com] } extensions: { firewall: { trusted_ips: [203.0.113.0/24] } } # settings for extensions, by name id: old hosts: [old.example.com] blocked: { status: 402, message: "Payment required" } Unknown hosts get 404 and no folder is ever created from a request. Ids are lowercase letters, digits, dots and dashes. Hosting platforms plug in their own InstanceSource (for example a control plane streaming the hostname - id map over SSE) instead of the file; a community mothership is one (the mothership section, ext/mothership). pocketone.yaml for a production host (each extension owns its section; every field has a default): server: https: ":443" http: ":80" # redirects to HTTPS (and answers ACME HTTP-01 challenges) plain: [] # extra plain-HTTP listeners (no TLS, no redirect), e.g. a private network other servers forward on tls: { cert: /path/fullchain.pem, key: /path/privkey.pem } # re-read when they change; or the autotls section multisite: {} instances: { file: ./instances.yaml } pocker: root: ./pb_root hooks_pool_size: 2 egress_allow: [] # private networks apps may still reach (default none) # default limits for every instance (each instance can override them, see below) max_js_execution: 30s # any single JS call (hook, route, cron, migration) max_js_allocation: 64MiB # one-shot JS allocations max_call_stack_size: 2000 max_sleep: 10s max_query_duration: 30s # any SQL statement without its own deadline http_send_max_timeout: 60s http_send_max_body: 10MiB max_concurrent_js: 16 # JS calls an instance runs at once; more wait up to max_js_execution, then fail rate_limits: # per client IP and per instance; trusted clients get the trusted set ip_hourly: 1000 instance_hourly: 10000 ip_concurrent: 15 instance_concurrent: 250 file_weight: 0.1 # a /api/files request costs a tenth trusted: { ip_hourly: 5000, instance_hourly: 20000, ip_concurrent: 50, instance_concurrent: 250 } # off: true # no rate limiting (the default in dev mode unless rate_limits is set) firewall: allow_cidrs: [] # peers allowed to connect (empty = everyone); others get 403 trusted_proxies: [] # peers whose client-IP headers are believed client_ip_headers: [CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP] trusted_clients: [] # client IPs with the trusted limits on every instance trusted_client_headers: [X-Client-IP] # a trusted client names its end user (own buckets) rate_limit_header_prefix: X-RateLimit # autotls: # automatic certificates (ACME, via CertMagic, Caddy's certificate engine) # auto: true # email: ops@example.com # ca: letsencrypt # letsencrypt (default), letsencrypt-staging, zerossl, or an ACME directory URL # storage: ./pb_root/.pocker-certs # domains: [" .example.com", "example.com"] # obtained up front; wildcards need dns # dns: { provider: cloudflare, api_token_env: CF_API_TOKEN } # only needed for wildcards Firewall (ext/firewall; on whenever the config has firewall or rate_limits ). Peers outside allow_cidrs get 403. The client IP comes from client_ip_headers only when the peer is a trusted proxy, otherwise it is the peer. Rate-limited requests get 429 with Retry-After and a message naming the limit; every routed response carries -{Ip,Instance}-{Hourly,Concurrent}-{Limit,Remaining} and -{Ip,Instance}-Hourly-Reset , listed in Access-Control-Expose-Headers . Long-lived responses (realtime) hold their concurrency slot until they end. TLS. Certificate files are core ( server.tls ). Automatic certificates are ext/autotls (its autotls section): with auto: true and no dns , every hostname the instance source maps gets its own certificate on its first TLS handshake (HTTP-01 / TLS-ALPN-01), with any DNS host and no API token; hostnames no instance serves never trigger issuance. A DNS provider (Cloudflare for now) is only needed for wildcard domains , proved through DNS-01; a wildcard without one is a config error. Each instance can override any of those limits (zero or missing fields keep the default): instances: id: shop hosts: [shop.example.com] limits: max_js_execution: 60s max_js_allocation: 128MiB id: api hosts: [api.example.com] access: { cors_origins: [https://app.example.com] } limits: { max_concurrent_js: 32 } extensions: firewall: { rate_limits: { ip_hourly: 5000, instance_concurrent: 500 }, trusted_ips: [203.0.113.0/24] }

title: Pocker
heading: Extensions
text: pocker.Provider.Extensions (or pocker.Server.Extensions in Go) takes extensions (see extension.go ). Each implements Name() and any of: extkit.Extension a PocketOne extension, registered on every instance's app before it bootstraps ( Register(app, cfg) ) with the instance's extensions. settings, its id in extkit.AppID(app) ; e.g. pitr, storage, tokens, s3redirect, mailrelay, bulkmail. enabled: false skips it for that instance. A change to an instance's extensions: settings restarts its app on its next request. The same value works on a single app. multisite.Extension a host extension ( RegisterHost ): it provides host contracts (gate/v1, tls/v1, http.wrap/v1, ...) as on any runtime (docs/extensions.md) Starter background work that needs pocker's Manager AppIniter host code that needs the whole Instance when setting up its app ( InitApp(inst, app) ); runs on every start, including restarts. Extensions use extkit.Extension instead, so they run on a single app too and pass the conformance test. Per-instance settings for an extension go under the instance's extensions. (read them with pocker.DecodeExtensionConfig ). app.Restart() (a backup restore, pitr) restarts only that instance, not the process. Timings for the Server-Timing header are registered with multisite.Timing(ctx, fn) . The stock pocketone binary runs pocker with mailtrap, and its host with servertiming and autotls ( multisite.Options.Extensions , the same under docker); the firewall turns on from its sections.

title: Pocker
heading: Platform values and logs
text: Superusers ( superusers: [{email, password_hash, id?, token_key?}] ) are upserted into the app's _superusers in Go when it starts, e.g. so a hosting platform's login works in the dashboard. Nothing goes through env. Private values ( private: {...} ) are for the host application's Go code and never visible to JS. A host registers that code with Server.SetupApp(inst, app) , which runs after migrations and before the app serves (for example a backup route checked against inst.Private["backup_token"] ). Secrets ( secrets: {...} ) are the instance's environment: what its JS sees through $os.getenv / process.env , and nothing else. No names are reserved; platform settings are explicit fields. Encryption key ( encryption_key ) encrypts the app's stored settings (like --encryptionEnv ). JS never sees it. Access ( access: {cors_origins} ) is the owner's say over which browser origins may call the instance (PocketBase matching: exact, , wildcards; empty = any). Client IPs that get the trusted rate limits are the firewall's extensions.firewall.trusted_ips (on top of the process-wide firewall.trusted_clients ). Extensions ( extensions: { : ...} ) are per-instance settings for extensions; extensions read them once, so changing them restarts the app on its next request. Logs: the app's own logs (the dashboard's Logs) are per instance in its pb_data . console. from JS hooks goes to /logs/exec.log as JSON lines {message, stream, time} ( stdout for log/info/debug, stderr for warn/error), rotated to exec.log.1 at 10 MiB. A start failure (e.g. a broken hooks file) is written there too, and only that instance fails. When an instance's secrets , encryption_key , access , limits , dev , dir , superusers , private or remote changes, its app restarts on the next request (the old one finishes in-flight requests first), so a rotated secret takes effect immediately. Host changes apply without a restart. GET /.well-known/health on any host reports {status, instances, running} . Changing an instance's files from host code (deploys, restores): Manager.WithInstanceStopped(ctx, id, fn) stops the app, holds new requests for that instance, runs fn(dir) , then lets them through to a fresh app. Manager.StartInstance(ctx, id) starts it right away and returns the start error (for example to tell a deploy that a hook is broken), Manager.Running(id) says whether it is started, and Manager.InstanceDir(id) gives its folder. Manager.Ready() says whether the instance list has loaded. Manager.LogInstance(id, stream, message) appends to the instance's logs/exec.log (e.g. a scheduled job's result). Host code that runs in its own goroutines gets the Manager from Server.OnStart , before any request is served. Several servers, one set of instances. An instance with remote: runs on another server: Pocker checks the peer and the instance's rate limits here, then forwards the request (a reverse proxy to the URL by default; Server.Forward replaces it, e.g. to hold requests while the other server restarts). Its app never starts here, and an app already running here stops when remote is set. plain_listen gives the other servers a plain-HTTP port on a private network, and Manager.Firewall() lets host routes in front of the Manager use the same peer check.

title: Pocker
heading: Sandbox
text: Every instance's JS hooks and migrations run in a sandbox (the sandbox extension), and its SQL runs behind SQLite's authorizer ( sandbox/sqlguard.go ). The sandbox extension also owns the egress policy ( sandbox/egress.go ); pocker turns it on for its instances. sandbox_test.go runs one attack per route from one instance against another instance and the host; all of these are refused: Files: $os. , $filepath.glob/walk , $filesystem.fileFromPath , $template.loadFiles , $apis.static , require() Confined to the instance folder with an os.Root : the kernel resolves every path beneath it, refusing .. and symlinks that leave it. Relative paths and absolute paths inside the folder ( __hooks + "/x" ) work as before. Host primitives: $os.cmd , $os.exec , $os.exit , $os.args , $filesystem.local Disabled ( $os.args is empty). Environment: $os.getenv , process.env Only the instance's own secrets . Go internals: $app.restart/bootstrap/runAllMigrations/onServe/onTerminate/onBootstrap/cron/unsafeWithoutHooks , hook.bindFunc/bind/trigger/unbind , sql.DB/Conn/Tx/Stmt (e.g. dbx.DB.DB() ), database/sql/driver , os/exec , net , syscall , http.Server controls Hidden from JS (the sandbox's member filter: they read as undefined , including when promoted from an embedded app type). Top-level onRecord , routerAdd , cronAdd and the rest of $app work as usual. Raw SQL ( $app.db().newQuery ) Allowed. SQLite's authorizer refuses ATTACH (and VACUUM INTO ) outside the instance's pb_data , PRAGMA temp_store_directory/data_store_directory and load_extension ; the CLI-only readfile / writefile / fsdir don't exist in the library. Statements without a deadline get max_query_duration . CPU Every JS call is interrupted after max_js_execution , Go calls included; sleep() is capped at 10 s. At most max_concurrent_js calls are in flight per instance. Memory Each instance has one QuickJS VM (ext/jsvm) with a hard cap (64 MiB by default): its JS heap plus the Go objects its JS holds. Growth past it, gradual or at once, is an out-of-memory error for that instance only. The JS stack is capped by size, so deep recursion is an error, never a crash. $os.readFile , fileFromPath and readerToString / toBytes are capped at max_js_allocation . Outbound network: $http.send , $filesystem.fileFromURL , S3 storage and backups, OAuth2/JWK fetches, SMTP Public addresses only, checked on the address actually connected to (after DNS, so rebinding doesn't help): loopback, private ranges, link-local and cloud metadata, CGNAT, multicast, reserved and documentation ranges, and IPv6 equivalents/IPv4-in-IPv6 are refused unless listed in egress_allow . Installed process-wide on Go's default HTTP transport and PocketBase's SMTP client ( pocker/egress.go ). Host code that must reach private addresses (e.g. a control plane over a private network) uses its own http.Client with its own transport. $http.send timeouts and response bodies are capped. Limits of the memory controls: Go objects JS holds are charged by estimate, and Go's garbage collector can let the process use up to about twice the charge; set GOMEMLIMIT for the process as the backstop. Not covered yet: per-instance concurrency limits, and OS-level defence in depth: run Pocker as a non-root user with an OS firewall that only lets that user reach public addresses (a second, independent egress layer), plus seccomp and Landlock.

title: Pocker
heading: Changes to PocketBase
text: These live in the repo root (PocketBase's own files), not in this extension. Kept small and marked // PocketOne: so upstream merges stay easy: core.BaseAppConfig.AppMigrations : a per-app migrations list (JS migrations from jsvm register there instead of the global core.AppMigrations ). core.BaseAppConfig.EncryptionKey : the settings encryption key passed in directly instead of read from the process environment. The JS engine isn't a core change: Pocker runs jsvm (QuickJS), an extension, and the sandbox plugs into it. PocketBase's own plugins/jsvm is exactly upstream's. Mail needs no core change: the sandbox sends an app's own SMTP through the egress policy on OnMailerSend ( sandbox.BindMail ).

title: Pocker
heading: Versions
text: PocketOne has its own version line, starting at v0.0.1 , independent of PocketBase's numbers. When PocketBase releases, we merge it and decide then how to bump ours. Each release says which PocketBase version it's based on. The module path stays ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase , so a build pins a PocketOne version through the replace line: replace ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase = github.com/pockethost/pocketone v0.0.1

title: Remotes
text: Version 0.0.1 · Owners: @benallfree Named remotes for the pocketone command: the apps a project deploys to, each signed in to once. Give an app a name like prod , log in, and commands such as pocketone deploy prod know where to go and who you are. pocketone remote add prod https://myapp.example.com pocketone login prod pocketone deploy prod # Deploy Install · Configure · Use · Integrations · Example

title: Remotes
heading: Install
text: Remotes is built into pocketone and on : the remote , login , logout and link commands are always there, and every app provides remote/v1: whoami at GET /api/_c/remote/v1 (so other machines can sign in to it), status, restart and logs. There's nothing to install: it's in the standard set. In your own Go build, use the standard set, or register it through its contracts yourself: app := pocketbase.New() extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{remotes.New(remotes.Config{})}, nil, nil) // remote/v1; on pocketbase.PocketBase also the commands app.Start() The module is github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/remotes . Add Tokens for API tokens and the OAuth server for browser login.

title: Remotes
heading: Configure
text: There is no pocketone.yaml section, flag or settings screen. Remotes keeps two files and reads a few environment variables.

title: Remotes
heading: The project's remotes
text: .pocketbase/remotes.json in the project holds names and URLs only, so commit it: {"default": "prod", "remotes": {"prod": {"url": "https://myapp.example.com"}}} Commands find it by walking up from the current folder. It isn't a pb_ name, since pb_ folders are deployed.

title: Remotes
heading: Saved logins
text: Logins are saved per user, keyed by URL, in ~/.config/pocketone/credentials.json (mode 0600). Set P1_CONFIG_DIR to use another folder; with XDG_CONFIG_HOME set, it's $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pocketone/ .

title: Remotes
heading: Environment variables
text: P1_TOKEN_ A token for one remote, for CI. The name is upper case, other characters as _ ( P1_TOKEN_PROD ). P1_TOKEN A token for any remote. P1_CONFIG_DIR Where saved logins are kept. A token in the environment wins over a saved login. Every PocketOne variable starts with P1_ , in every build (the pockethost binary reads P1_TOKEN too). The pocketone folder comes from the command's name, so a build shipped under another name keeps its logins apart ( ~/.config/pockethost ).

title: Remotes
heading: Manage remotes
text: pocketone remote add prod https://myapp.example.com --default pocketone remote list # names, URLs and who you're logged in as; marks the default pocketone remote default prod pocketone remote rm staging # the saved login stays; see logout pocketone remote whoami prod # who you are there, your token's scopes, and what the app offers A URL without a scheme gets https:// . The first remote you add becomes the default. A command that names no remote uses the default, else the only remote, else the one called default . Any command also takes a URL in place of a name: pocketone deploy https://other.example.com .

title: Remotes
heading: Log in
text: pocketone login prod login tries, in order (the command itself never asks for a password): The browser , when the remote runs the OAuth server. Your browser opens, you sign in and approve, and the command finishes. Over SSH or without a display it shows a code to enter on another device instead; --device asks for that, and --no-browser prints the URL without opening it. A pasted token ( pbt_... , a PocketHost token, or a PocketBase auth token). At the prompt, paste it, or pass --token or --token-stdin . A browser login keeps a refresh token and renews itself when it's within a day of expiring. You'll see Logged in to https://myapp.example.com as admin@example.com (oauth).

title: Remotes
heading: Link in one step
text: pocketone link https://myapp.example.com pocketone link https://myapp.pockethost.io ph_pat_... link adds the remote (named default , or --name ), makes it the default if there's none yet, and logs in. It takes the same login flags.

title: Remotes
heading: Log out
text: pocketone logout prod Forgets the saved login. A browser login is also revoked on the remote (its refresh token); a pasted token stays valid until you revoke it in the dashboard. If the remote can't be reached, it tells you to revoke it in the dashboard.

title: Remotes
heading: Works with
text: Deploy deploy , dev and pull resolve their remote and login through Remotes and find deploy/v1 in whoami's contracts; restart and logs use remote/v1. OAuth (in Tokens) Provides oauth/v1, so whoami lists it; login then signs in through the browser (loopback redirect on 127.0.0.1 with PKCE) or a device code. Tokens Provides the API tokens login takes when pasted. Whoami reports a token's id and scopes.

title: Remotes
heading: remote/v1
text: Remote control of an app, at /api/_c/remote/v1 : whoami GET /api/_c/remote/v1 none needed (any token may ask who it is) status GET /api/_c/remote/v1/status remote:read restart POST /api/_c/remote/v1/restart remote logs GET /api/_c/remote/v1/logs?n=100 (server-sent events) remote:read Whoami says who the request's credential is and what the app offers, so clients can discover it: {"auth": {"collection": "_superusers", "id": "…", "email": "admin@example.com"}, "via": "token", "tokenId": "…", "scopes": ["deploy", "remote"], "contracts": ["deploy/v1", "oauth/v1", "remote/v1", "tokens/v1"], "extensions": ["tokens", "remotes", "deploy"], "app": {"name": "Acme", "url": "https://myapp.example.com"}} via is token for an API token, jwt for a PocketBase auth token, and empty with no credential ( auth is then null , and extensions is left out). contracts are the contract APIs the app offers, each at /api/_c/ / : everything a client can use (oauth/v1's metadata is at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server ). Restart answers at once and restarts just after (under Pocker, only that instance).

title: Remotes
heading: Building on Remotes
text: remote/v1 client. remotev1.NewClient(url, token, httpClient) (ext/contracts/remote/v1) calls whoami, status, restart and logs. Go client. The CLI client lives with the contract, in remoteclient (ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient), so other extensions' commands use it without importing this one. remoteclient.Open(dir, name) resolves a remote and its credential (environment first, then the saved login, renewing a browser login when due) and returns a remoteclient.Client : base URL, bearer token, an HTTP client with short connect timeouts, and JSON , NewRequest , Do and Whoami . It also holds the linked project ( LoadProject ), saved logins ( LoadCredentials ) and the sign-ins ( LoginWithToken , OAuthLogin ). Deploy's commands build on it. Commands. remotes.Commands() returns the remote , login , logout and link commands, for a binary that isn't a pocketbase.PocketBase . The rest of remote is generated: every operation of every contract the binary links is a remote ... command (cli.commands/v1), such as remote status , remote restart , remote restore to --at -2h . Login. remotes.BrowserLogin is the sign-in login tries first ( remoteclient.OAuthLogin ; tests replace it).

title: Remotes
heading: Example
text: example/main.go is an app with remotes and API tokens. Run two copies and add one as a remote of the other; its comment has the commands. // Command example is a PocketOne app with remotes and API tokens: run two copies, add one as a remote of the other's // project and sign in. // // go run ./example serve --http=127.0.0.1:8090 # the "remote" // go run ./example remote add local http://127.0.0.1:8090 # in a project folder // go run ./example login local # browser sign-in: admin@example.com / password // go run ./example remote whoami // // Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password. package main import ( "log" "ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/remotes" "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/tokens" ) func main() { app := pocketbase.New() devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password" // registered through their contracts (the standard set does this for you): remotes provides remote/v1 (whoami at // /api/_c/remote/v1, status, restart, logs) and the remote/login/logout/link commands; tokens adds API tokens // and the OAuth server login signs in through if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{tokens.New(tokens.Config{}), remotes.New(remotes.Config{})}, nil, nil); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } if err := app.Start(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } }
